title: Nice but could be better
body:
So I bought this years ago but never used it and was checking out another app and figured I’d use this and compare it. What I would like to see here is device syncing. Calendar and Apple health integration for reading and exercise habits and with the calendar it can set you reminders and adjust if schedules change. A disappointment is that there’s no pre set habit for showers. Ok but not even an icon? There’s a duster icon but not one for a shower? There’s even a tooth icon for brushing teeth but no shower when many many depressed Americans don’t shower. I’m tracking cold showers btw not regular ones but anyways. I can’t remember what I paid but I couldn’t justify the current subscription cost for how basic it is and the features it lacks that other apps have. I know these guys have been around awhile so I’m hoping they continue to improve it and get ahead on the AI train. Oh one final thing. Because it doesn’t play well with Apple my size settings don’t transfer to the app and there is no way to make things larger. I can see and read most stuff with a little difficulty but some text is too small to read and. I ability to enlarge text to make it more readable but that’s not going to be a common issue for most but blind people use apps too lol

Edit: dark mode all the time is getting old quick. There is no bright light mode when I wake up and the dark mode widget looks really dumb during the day next to everything else not in dark mode.

title: Exactly what I was looking for
body:
I wanted an app that would let me set daily goals, but also goals that could be 3x per week at my discretion which day or on set days. I didn't think there would be an app that would perfectly meet my needs, but this one does. Perfect and worth the 3.99 for the paid app that lets you have more than five reminders.

Update after lots of use: The only reason I dropped my rating to five stars is that really often when I check off a task it stays frozen, that is shifted right with the check mark displayed. I have eight habits and it never makes it through all eight without freezing. To get it to register that the habit was done I need to hard close the app and relaunch it. That is a small daily annoyance that I end up doing a couple times each day. 

Besides that, in terms of function and design, this is by far the best app I’ve found, which is why I stick with it despite the minor annoyance of having to hard close it to register which habits are checked off.

title: Great App but Expensive
body:
I have used this app premium version for two months now. It has been amazing. It is exactly what I need. A habit tracker where I can actually analyze the data to see which habits I still need to work on. 

I gave it 4 stars because I’ve been having issues with its timer feature. If I turn on the timer and move to another app, the timer stops working. If I play music or a video, the timer stops working. It’s very frustrating especially since I like using its Pomodoro feature to complete tasks. It throws my data off. 

Another feature that needs to be fixed is displaying data if you completed some of the work. There are some goals that are time based. For example, if the goal is 30 minutes a day, but you only completed 20 minutes. It would be nice to see it in the stats section. You only see if it is completed or not on the calendar even though you have a symbol for some done. 

Additionally, I wish I could export my data to an excel file. If I’m tracking my goals this would take it to the next level.

I know that many have complained about the price increase. I am paying about $35 a year for it. This is pricey but I think it’s worth it. Now if it jumps up to $80 that would be really steep.

title: “Mark a habit as incomplete”
body:
I think there should be a feature where you can mark that a habit was not completed. There is a feature where you can skip a habit in special occasions, and there is a feature where you can mark that a habit was completed. I understand that if you don’t do either of these then the app recognizes it as an incomplete habit but sometimes when I go back to previous days and see that a habit is not completed, I can’t remember if I just forgot to mark it as complete or if I actually didn’t do it. That’s why I really think there should be a feature to mark that a habit was not completed instead of just having that be recognized by the app if you don’t mark it at all. I don’t want to just skip a habit and have it say that my streak continues. I benefit from the punishment of losing a streak. That’s why I want there to be an additional feature to mark that a habit was not completed. Maybe it could be a long press on the habit or some other type of gesture. 

Thank you for your time and for considering this feature. Other than this feature, I would actually give five stars—but this is a huge issue for me that is make or break for me.

title: Account/Subscription Management is Non-Existent
body:
The core of this app is sound. It helps keep me on track with my productivity and habits when it works. Having said that, there are many flaws on this app that make me regret getting a subscription. 
1. There is no cross device functionality for my account. The habits you create and track only exist on the device in which you created them. So I can’t track my activity on, say, my iphone if I mainly use my ipad to track my habits. I assume the developers don’t want to spend the resources for backend storage and account management. Either that or they’re simply unable.
2. Related to above, there is no central place to manage my account or even tell which account a device is logged in under. When I select the manage subscription item in settings it tells me to log into the apps site to manage, but the website offers no such ability to manage anything.
3. The Pomodoro tracker is absolutely atrocious. It is completely useless. The timer won’t continue to count down most times when you minimize the app. So you will long be done with your first phase when opening the app only to see that hardly ten seconds have passed since you last minimized. I strongly suspect this is developer error(relying on background running when ios can kill it at anytime, vs. using local notifications). Hint: Use remote notifications for this when/if you get a backend running.

The design and UI flow is really great, however, this apps potential is being limited by these severe issues. 

At this time I cannot recommend this app to anybody.

title: Almost the best, but behind on the times
body:
This app genuinely might be the best at handling habits right now, but it is seriously missing a feature that modern apps really need to be functional for the modern productivity-minded individual: syncing across devices! If you’ve got a great set of habits built for yourself on the iPad, but then leave the house and think you’ll be able to track those habits on your iPhone or Apple Watch, you’ll be sadly mistaken. And that’s a huge drawback when you are someone that relies on a wide variety of devices in various locations to get your daily things done. After researching other options, I will be switching until this necessary feature is implemented and no longer hindering workflow or habit tracking.

other suggestions include:
-being able to mark additional times you completed a habit beyond the goal number
-ability to split screen with other apps

title: Where’s my subscription details?
body:
I have been using Productive since 2016 but NEVER, mind you, gathered myself to stay accountable.

End of last year, I decided to change that. Habits were looking good. I changed my phone and reinstalled the app.

To my utter disappointment, all my data was gone! To my surprise I couldn’t even find my subscription on Apple. So how was I on Premium (how I know is because I was able to add unlimited habits), but not have them synced ANYWHERE?!

I reached out to support, and they just apologized and repeated what I told them. No resolution.

Regardless, I restarted my habits and I’ve been going strong till now, but I’m so afraid that I’m gonna lose all of this, whenever I change my phone again. For this reason, I’m very disappointed.

And somewhere, via some email, I know I am being charged, and for the life of me, they’re not able to tell me where it’s going from. How am I supposed to know when they don’t even know? This is super disappointing!

But on the flipside, I’m obsessed with the app, and I love how easily I can track my habits. Yet, I’m reconsidering another app due to paranoia from the above reasons.

title: confusing at first
body:

all it does is create a block in which you swipe to mark complete. i'm trying to use this to help myself at work to keep on top of stuff.
it as a pomodoro timer but i was hoping to find an organizer that times my tasks so i know how long it takes me to complete said task. I'd definitely like to see two separate tabs for work and home so it doesn't feel clustered and overwhelming. it ruins the point of having a list if i'm overwhelmed trying to figure out my own list. it's at least separated by time of day which helps a lot. and i can at least color code and change symbols to represent the taks at hand (as in green suitcase for work) though i would still rather it be a separate tab than getting it miked in with my entire morning routine.

if there was a function for time blocks to help better plan what i could realistically do i'd give it four stars. and if i could separate work from home rather than have just color code id give it 5 stars for both.

im not sure if a 34 dollar subscription is going to be worth it. if it was halve the cost or had more functions i might keep it than. 
the overall User Interface is very friendly and i hope it would never change. it's easy to add, create and get notified at the exact time you want to start a task.
it's great for starting small habits to be a healthier person, but i don't think it was designed to help organize work loads

title: Pomodoro Limitations
body:
I wanted to love this app. It was everything I was looking for - a pomodoro with all the added features a girl with ADHD like me can appreciate. I spent a bunch of time creating schedules for work and school time (I both work and attend school from home). It was really cool to block out my whole day AND have the nifty extra challenges on offer. 
Then I quickly discover that the pomodoro will stop running whenever a notification pops up. Every. Single. Notification. Do you get a lot of notifications? You do?! Wow, me too!
Having to pay attention to all of those notifications and then go on to the Productive app to restart my timer? Lol. Kinda defeats the purpose!
I wrote the Productive team and got a stock ‘thanks for your feedback’ answer in return, indicating that there is no solution at this time. Really sorry I wasted money on an app that will actually limit my productivity. Womp womp.

title: Excellent, with a few bugs.
body:
I have never, and I seriously mean never, brushed my teeth and flossed for more than a week straight. I've tried all sorts of things, but I'm very proud to say that I am currently on a 45 day streak of brushing both day and night, flossing, and using mouthwash, and I think a lot of that is due to this app.

I've been using the premium version of this app for around a year now, and I'm very happy with it. It's intuitive, simple, customizable, and the sound effects are great at reinforcing the reward of completing habits.

My only complaint is with some errors regarding habits that aren't daily. Any time I've tried to add weekly habits, or really anything that isn't daily, it messes with my streak and will end it even if I've completed everything. The streak is really important in motivating me, and so I've ended up just removing all my weekly habits, which isn't ideal.

In spite of that, I highly recommend downloading this app and trying the premium version.

title: It’s fine. Too easy to ignore it. Should be more annoying.
body:
I am a full time college student with ADHD and narcolepsy, so needless to say it is very difficult for me to remember to do literally anything even with the truckload of medications I have to take. I was curious about this app because it seems to have good reviews. Don’t get me wrong, I do like this app quite a bit: especially the built in pomodoro timer which is very useful for homework. However it is too easy for me to forget about this app because it doesn’t remind me to use it often enough. 

I have found myself ignoring the app for several days before remembering to use it again. I wish there were an option to make it send you lots of notifications over and over until a certain task is completed. I need more than just one reminder notification which I can easily swipe away and then continue procrastinating.  

For example, I always forget to brush my teeth so I wish there was a more forceful and annoying reminder/productivity app that could make my phone send me hundreds of notifications over and over every morning until I do it.

I think for a person with a normal level of executive functioning this app is fine as it is, after all most people wouldn’t need their phone to vibrate and make noises incessantly until they remember to brush their teeth every morning. 

But I really wish it had the option to send nonstop reminders until a task is completed, for those of us who are very sleepy and forgetful and need an extra push to be able to build a consistent daily routine.

title: developers please read!
body:
after testing extensively over several hours other habit tracking apps I found this one to be the most fully featured in terms of statistics and things like an in app timer. The widgets are clean and good enough, there is a more section, and the ability to pause habits. However there are some major shortcomings of this app that has been available for so long that I think would make it much better. 
1. overflow timer - would be very appreciated. It’s very difficult to edit entries to show the time that was spent versus the time that was scheduled in the habit. also, it doesn’t show the edited time in the statistics after the fact. I would love to be able to set the timer to start for example minutes read and if my time exceeds what was scheduled it would automatically update and show in statistics.
2. bad habits -there is no proprietary bad habit set up in the app as of now. It’s easy enough to mark don’t smoke as completed if you don’t smoke for that day. But what if it is some thing like cut back smoking and you want to mark every time you have a cigarette so that that data is available in statistics and so that if you are trying to cut down from 10 cigarettes a day you can see when you only had nine and passed your habit but also when you only had three and did even better-even so when you failed the habit and had 11 but when you also failed the habit and had 20.

thanks guys!

title: Has a lot of room for improvement
body:
The app is good at what it says it does, but there are huge gaps to its functionalities. With a set of 3 daily habits, if you forget to mark one of them as Done (or Skipped), you can forget about timed reminders you have set up for any task the next day. Only if you complete a day do you get reminded the next day - that means the initial stages of building a habit are made harder by this app. That’s a bad approach. Saw last night’s notification this morning and used it to mark the task done for last night? Nope, you marked it done for tonight. 

EDIT: The point below is wrong, there is indeed a way to create a task that repeats every Sunday. The option for that is under “Daily” and not “Weekly”, which is why it was a little difficult to find. 

~~If you wish to have a weekly task that needs to be done on a certain day, forget about it - no way to set up that sort of task on this app.~~

title: From a Paying Customer

I haven’t either. I bet there’s no YouTube videos on it, considering this app is NOT 80,000 RECIEWS STRONG like that, or popular like that, in any way! My original review when I first started with it; ‘Takes some playing around with to fully understand how to make it work for you. I forget what the cost of membership was but to know how many times I did a certain thing has been worth it. The features I’m not all that into but the interface is really easy to look at.’

I use it for self-improvement and it keeps me honest with my progress. 

Pros: Group challenges to try new habits, great scheduling options for various habits, enough progress stats (for me at least)

Cons:
 1) Would LOVE to have family sharing option. 
2) Would be great to challenge friends/family who also use this app.  The group challenges are a great idea but you complete them individually.
3) syncing across personal devices is not an option or available as far as I found. 

All in all it’s a great app. I have found it helpful and dare I say I have improved personally since I started using this app. If you are looking for a task manager or scheduler look elsewhere.

What I’m disappointed with this app is the inability to save my data to the cloud. I have an iPhone where I mainly work on my habits and receive alerts for. But I also have an iPad that I would like to use for looking at me progress and creating new habits, but it is not possible to login with the same credentials and see the data that is on my phone, that is not possible, because the data is stored local to my phone. Additionally, I have a concern with not having this capability built into the app, because of I ever lose my phone, or it malfunctions, I won’t be able to restore all of my saved habits and data. This is a core feature of almost all my other apps I have. 

This cloud sync feature is important to me, so I plan to evaluate other habit apps from the App Store.

title: Super Useful App
body:
I’ve been using the Productive app for a few months now and I’m enjoying it so far. It’s nice to see you progress on habits and for me it’s an opportunity to recognize what I accomplished today. I can be a little hard on myself sometimes so it’s nice to spend some time looking at what I did do versus what I didn’t.
That being said there’s a few things I think would be a major improvement to the app.
1. A way to either organize a the order that you see your habits so that you can easily follow a thought out routine. Even better would be a way to group habit based off specific routines (ie morning/evening routines, pre-workout routine, cleaning routine, study routine etc)
2. A goal setting interface. I think habits and goals work together. Often bigger goals require completing a task on a regular bases.  I imagine a goal page that shows all of a persons big goals, under the bigger goals would be smaller goals or single tasks that lead towards the larger goal and the habits that contribute. For example one of my personal goals is to push 300lbs on the leg press. On a goal page I would be reminded of that specific goal everyday and then I could click it and see all the milestones (like hit 240lbs, then 250lbs etc) that lead up to that goal as well as a single tasks related to the goal (for example: research proper nutrition for improved strength training) and all the habits I’m doing to achieve that goal (like workout, stretch, drink water etc).
3. More icons for habits also would be cool.
Overall genuinely enjoy the app and would like to keep using it. Just had some ideas on how to improve the user experience. Everything it does include is amazing. Challenges, articles, widgets, and the habit stats are invaluable.

title: So Much Potential. Needs Updates
body:
Love this app. Best one I’ve found by far. I’m a premium member. The interface is nice, it’s easy to use. However, there are a few areas that I needs improvement in. I’ve listed below as what it needs to have and what it could offer:

NEED -

- Per week, month, and year options. Currently you can only do per day. What if I say I want to practice yoga “twice per week” or “meditate 90 minutes per week”. Only way to do this now is to create a habit for the yoga and tie it to two specific days and complete them on those days. I don’t care about some habits occurring on a specific day as long as I do them that week.

- Reset on habits when making changes should be optional. This one is a killer and SO ANNOYING. Currently, if you make any changes whatsoever to the habit it resets your progress. What if I’m exercising Monday and Wednesday and I want to add Friday? Yep. That will reset your streak. Even though I’m ADDING another day to my habit (the opposite of failing) you lose your streak. Really lame design. 

Want

-additional colors or slider option
- add more than one line to description

title: The Best Habit App (for me, personally)
body:
I I have tried a great many habit-tracking / goal-reaching apps in an effort to inject some accountability into my journey towards being a more productive person.  But like New Years resolutions and the friends you made in High School, they all kind of fall away after the honeymoon period of “Wow, look how much work I’m putting into myself, yay me” wears off.

This app is, for me, not like that.  I’ve fallen off the bandwagon many times—for sure—but I always come back.  Maybe it’s the icons and the minimalist-but-with-depth design philosophy, maybe it’s the way features keep being added (maybe it’s the infuriating choice to push a subscription model… Probably not that), but Productive is just eminently charming and friendly.

It’s the perfect middle ground between overwhelmingly dense, all-in-one productivity/reminders/scheduling apps like ToDoist or Due and hyper open-ended checklist simulator apps like Clear or Bear.  ‘Productivity - Habit Tracker’ makes me happy to start and maintain habits.

(Disclaimer: none of this may apply to you; hacking your brain is a science of one—you do you!  Find what works!)
author: Ink Runner

title: App Makers Have Lost Focus
body:
I used to love, love, love this app. It had a gorgeous, simple design that was the epitome of iOS elegance. And it worked perfectly as a habit tracker.

Now the app is completely bloated. Instead of just tracking whatever habits you choose, now it has pop-up animations that encourage you to build on your success by taking on more habits. It also suggests challenges for things like fitness and intermittent fasting, all in the service of getting you to take on more habits. And the last straw for me is it now recommends articles about habits, seemingly to get you to take on more habits.

I don’t want any of these things, and I definitely don’t want an app that I use only to track very specific creativity and mental health habits to suggest that my real problem is that I’m not doing enough intermittent fasting! Instead of feeling good about tracking the things I want to accomplish, I feel the app now just reminds me that I’m not doing enough to “be better.” Instead of being self-directed, the app feels now like it has a perfect “me” in mind and will keep pushing me toward that hollow ideal.

This app is supposed to help you stay focused and get things done, but now it’s just a distraction to me. I used to use this every day and now I don’t want to open it at all.

title: Okay...
body:
So I started using this app a month ago and went for the year long subscription. I thought that a lot of the problems I was running into would be fixed with the subscription but they are still there. You get to add more tasks but every time I edit a task, even just the name of it, it makes it a new task and moves it to a different spot on a list. Which is annoying cause then I have to move it back manually and I lose all my data on the task. Just cause I move my reading time down from 20 min to 15 doesn’t mean that I dropped my streak and I would really like it to stay the same task. If it’s under the same task it should stay the same task! 

Also idk why the techies would get rid of the “do this many times function and then we will take it off the list”! That was the best function cause then I would get reminded for stuff I needed to do but had more time to do it rather than something I needed to do everyday.

I do like that they added more colors... should have been a given but I’ll take progress. 

Kinda disappointed in the money I spent and this is what I’m stuck with for the next year. OH AND WHEN THEY UPDATE YOU LOSE SOME TASKS THAT DONT FIT WITH THE NEW UPDATE! So I forgot to sign up for important classes and missed the deadline cause I put it in here and it didn’t remind me. :( 

It’s okay for daily reminders but not great for goal setting or for individual tasks. So if you looking to use this for school or anything like that go somewhere else. And if you find something good please lmk🥺 unless this app gets it together. Maybe the techies could create two different sections (1 for daily tasks and one for projects that are due in the future but still show up somewhere on the list like a “looking ahead” section.)

author: jeeves78

title: They need to learn about User Experience
body:
I have been using and paying for this app for a while, and it does what I need if I set all the settings right, although I’m annoyed that they keep popping things up every few months to try out some new feature, as if I’ll say, “Yeah, this system I’ve set up for myself has kept my life on track for the past few years, but let’s shake it up and try something else just for fun!” I wouldn’t complain if it was just a thing saying, “Hey, we added this new feature, want to try it?”, but usually the screen only has one button that takes you into the screen to start adding some new kind of habit (like the Challenges).

I recommended this to my mom a year or so ago, and I was shocked at how much the onboarding process has gone downhill. It prompted twice to buy the app before even showing her a tutorial that forced her to add a habit she wasn’t interested in, mark it done, undo it, etc, and then it prompted so often to pay for it in that first day, that she didn’t use it and decided not to pay for it.

Yesterday I sent an email to report a bug. I got a response today from their tech support trying to get the bug to resolve on my phone by reinstalling rather than tackling the actual bug, and so I instead installed the app on a new device to reproduce it, since their history with maintaining user data is pretty poor and I was not going to risk losing all my data over a bug I could work around.

But onboarding experience is even worse now. It took me like 5 minutes to just get into the app, and I ended up force quitting and reopening the app to get out of the tutorial. I was prompted 3 times during the onboarding/tutorial to pay for the app before I’d gotten a chance to try out the free side of the freemium model (as far as they knew since it was on a new device), and then as I tried to test the bug, I was interrupted several times by the pop up to pay for the full version.

So I no longer recommend this app. It’s trash. I think it’s bad enough that it’s worth me making an app for myself for what I want out of this. (Not to mention that the streaks don’t even mean anything since historical data often randomly gets gaps inserted that weren’t there the day before, breaking long running streaks. I’ve never missed one of these for the past 706 days, and I haven’t changed my habits for 437 days, and yet my overall streak is only 411 days. It’s clear the developers either don’t use the app, or they only use it to look for bugs and don’t actually care about it.

To the devs: if all the extra prompts to pay are an attempt to convert more people from free to paid, you’re going about it wrong. One prompt during the tutorial, cutting down the tutorial to just a couple screens, and then waiting to prompt for at least a couple days would convert more free users into paid users because they would get a chance to try the app first, and they might actually like it if they get a chance to try it. Prompting multiple times before they get a chance to use the app will either push them away or at best (for you) get someone to pay who doesn’t actually use the app, which is obviously morally wrong.

title: Good but annoying!
body:
So here’s the deal - I tried the app for a week. I actually really liked it based on function and all that, and I would say it was successful in helping me complete the habits I was looking to complete and track.

My issue is with the way overly persistent upgrade popups almost every time you click anything in the app, and that they went subscription based. Literally every 15 seconds of use in the app, you’ll see a full screen pop up asking you to upgrade. A)Way too much of our world has become subscription based! Its great for profits but it’s crap for consumers much of the time. I don’t need another leach with auto draft capabilities on my bank account. B)I don’t need syncing which means I don’t need to interact with servers, which is half a developer’s explanation for subscriptions usually. C)I’m happy to buy apps that are expensive even if it’s a one time purchase. I’ve even spent upwards of $50 and $100 on productivity apps in the past. But I got to use the version I bought for as long as I wanted - it wasn’t a recurring subscription.

Unless it’s truly an ongoing service like Netflix or Apple Music, or Dropbox, I’m not willing to engage a subscription.

So I like the app a lot, but won’t be using it and will look for others. And if I can’t find one, I’ll use paper or a spreadsheet on my phone.

This is a crazy-expensive app sub. I personally am not a big fan of the design, but it’s the unconscionable 🗓 subscription price 💵 for what you’re getting that really turns me off. If you got lots of extra bucks to blow every year, then go for it.

title: It’s fine. But annoying.
body:
The entire app is set up to be some silly competition with yourself. I just need something to keep track of the things I want to try and hit in a day — I’m not trying to guilt trip myself because my “streak is broken.” There doesn’t seem to be a way to turn this off, which is absurd. So it’s a great interface and user-friendly that way, but if you’re not interested in feeling bad about yourself every day when it brow-beats you for not completing your “habits,” I’d look elsewhere.

ETA: I was feeling pretty cranky when I tapped this review out, but as my year subscription comes to an end, I still won’t be renewing. I appreciate the response that some things can be turned off, but respectfully — most of them can’t be. And the edits that are offered often don’t work. Trying to update days that you’d like existing habits to appear on your list is hit or miss (usually miss — it doesn’t stick. I end up having to delete habits entirely and enter them anew to make any changes at all). The orientation of the app is toward creating new daily habits and competing with yourself. If that’s your thing, do it up. But if the developers want this to be for a wider audience, then group all of those notifications into a “challenge” interface, and give the rest of us an option to turn it off. I’d love this to be a task-tracker without the game aspect, but it isn’t.

If there was an update to add alarms and annoying notifications I would definitely come back to this app.

title: Glitches, crashes, poor sync across devices
body:
I’ve been using this app for about a year and half now and I’ve had many problems. Nothing just works how its supposed to. My completed tasks aren’t being synced across my devices, so if I click completed on my Apple Watch or iPhone, my iPad won’t reflect it, and vice versa. Sometimes it will sync one completion here or there but its very unreliable. I can mark every task completed on my iPad and hours later my iPhone has only realized I’ve completed one or two tasks. My devices haven’t even synced some completions from a month ago. This defeats the purpose of having it on separate devices if they won’t sync properly... as well as the whole idea of tracking habits.

On to the next problem: the sometimes working Apple Watch app. Probably 50% of the time the Apple Watch app is non-responsive or just crashes when you open it. I’ve had days where I can’t open the app on the Apple Watch. Yes... everything is updated and my settings are set to sync across devices... things just don’t work. I can’t believe I’ve paid for two years of service that works this poorly.

EDIT: Now even a year later it still is not syncing anything between my devices. In fact, I don’t even see an iCloud option in the settings anymore. I think they gave up on the syncing.

title: Great app w/room for improvement
body:
I’ve had this app for years and have used it on and off, it helps me get on track and I recommend it.
I really like the app for keeping track of all the daily things I want to get done, and especially things I’d like to do only once a week or month, like calling my grandmother and taking the time to plan my month out at the beginning of each month. 
I can check them off and then won’t be reminded again until the next week or month. 
It’s easy enough to use. 
I just have one rather large problem with it. It can be really discouraging the way it only gives you credit for “perfect days.” I just started the habit of drinking 8 glasses of water each day, I’ve achieved 5 glasses, 7 glasses etc, but in my stats, it’s like I drank no water at all. It’s really dissatisfying. 
A big motivation for me is feeling accomplished when I can see what I’ve done.
This app would be perfect if it notified me “you’ve completed 50% of your morning habits today! Keep it up!” Or if I could see I’ve almost reached my 8 full glasses of water almost every day this week.
With how I use the app, it’s almost impossible to achieve a perfect day, but it’d be nice to see that I keep up with over 70% of my daily habits each week. Or I do 100% of my nighttime habits.
That’s something I would change, along with how sensitive the buttons are, I’m always accidentally swiping habits left or right when I’m just scrolling through them. It’s annoying.

title: Invasive privacy policy - glad it lost all my data
body:
I used to love this app. Nice UI and great use of icons. I even paid for the premium features.

Then after the last update, ALL my data was lost. Habits, prefs, all gone. It found my Premium status, but lost everything else.

So I had to delete the app and reinstall. When it walked through the setup, I decided to read the privacy policy. And wow, I’m glad I did. 

IMO, this app collects far more personal data than is needed for a habit-tracking app. Personal info, browsing, location, and more — even your unique device identifiers — AND SHARES IT. They’re part of a “family” of companies and share your data between them and with partners. And I couldn’t find any way to opt out.

If someone needs to take meds, or exercise, or anything personal at all, I’m not okay with knowing they’re potentially sharing or selling my info to companies and ad networks and who knows what else.

Productive has become unreasonably expensive for what it does. It’s just a habit tracker. And with their very invasive privacy policy, I won’t be using it. Make your own call, of course, but I urge you to read it. I deleted Productive, and will be looking at apps that specify that your information does not leave your device.

title: An app created by sadists
body:
Update: I have written to customer support 5 times and they still have not resolved this issue. The most recent time is 12/13/2020. 

With this app if you don’t meet your goals this app tells you that you didn’t succeed and it suggests that you change your goals. It sends this message every —single — time you miss even one goal. It does it over and over again. I wrote to customer service for help. I asked them how to turn off the discouraging message. And their answer was “we’ll consider making that change in future upgrades.” Which, I guess is something. In the meantime they have made my money be wasted.

This is what I wrote to customer service on the 5th try on 12/13/2020:

I hate being told repeatedly by this app that my goal “streak” is broken. It isn’t. I just didn’t put it in the app. It’s a negative thing to say and it discourages my being productive. 

It’s a big thumbs down just when I’m opening my app to be productive. 

Please don’t write back again and say how you’ll let the developers know my feedback. Please try to get me a target date for fixing this. 

I paid good money for this app years ago and I really like it. It does exactly what I want. Except for this nasty, negative message that the developers added in 2019. 

Every time I get that negative comment about my streak being broken from this app it puts me in a sour mood. And I wanted to reach out and let the company that produces it know. This productivity app is harming my my ability to be productive.

body: Not very organized. If you set up a habit then that just goes to your daily tracker where everything is kept.  It’s a long laundry list of things to do.  It would be helpful to have the ability to categorize your list.  So, when I open “today” I might see the category of “lose 50lbs” and then inside of that all the things I need to do today to reach that goal. Also, they do have “challenges” that you can join that is similar to what I’m referencing above but there does seem to be a way to create a custom challenge or even to just remove the ones that they have.  It would be nice to have full control to customize what I want to do.

title: I Love it but Glitches Make it a Chore to Use
body:
I do really love this app. I use it as motivation to get things done when my depression extinguishes all self-motivation. I immediately subscribed to it and would have rated 5 stars in that first month. 

When I first got the app a few months ago I noticed a couple of small glitches that weren’t really problematic and just restarting the app fixed them. If you slide to complete one task quickly after another, two of the first task will appear in the completed tasks instead of the two separate ones. Sometimes the app lags when I’m trying to complete a task so I have to slide it multiple times and that can result in the above happening; which is frustrating because I have to restart the app to be able to undo that second task that I haven’t done yet. Little mildly frustrating glitches like that. They have been getting progressively more common to the point that I now have to restart the app three to four times every singe time I use it. It’s almost non-functional.

The reason I’m here on the App Store today looking for a replacement for this app and leaving this review is because of a new glitch that made its appearance a couple day ago. If I edit a task, even without saving the changes I’ve made, it turns on the “Set end date or total amount” function and I can’t turn it off. This makes it to where the next time you complete that task it automatically removes it from your habits. Luckily it can be salvaged and reinstated but doing so resets all of the data on that habit making it brand new. I have “solved” this by setting the end date of all of my tasks as Dec 31, 2099. That was exhausting and infuriating. It took nearly an hour to do and reset all of my habits back to new as if I’d never done a single thing in the three months I’ve had this app. Now I need to make more habits but do not want to have to do that for all of them.

That glitch was the final straw, I cannot continue using this app until it is fixed. Productive, as it is currently, is practically unusable and attempting to use it just results in anger. I am incredibly disappointed that I’m having to switch to something else because I adore Productive.

body: I’ve been using this app for years, and paid for premium back when it was a flat fee. I want to make it clear that the app itself has really helped me a lot with my ADHD and overall executive function, and the flat fee (not subscription) has been worth it. However the fact that the app is completely unusable (wont even open!) for like a week or more after each update is unreal. I figured out that this was the case years ago, so have consistently delayed updating for at least a few weeks after each update release on habit (ha). However, I accidentally updated a mere week after release this time....and now the app once again won’t even open for me. While forgivable for a fairly new product team, it’s crazy that this is still the case ~a week after an update years later. Why not roll back a version so we at least have something workable to use in the meantime? Also don’t release updates until they’ve been extensively verified and tested for bugs.

title: Good app but could be better
body:
I really do like this app to keep track of certain habits, but it could be better. 

1. There is no way to edit the frequency of a habit. For instance, in the beginning I wanted to workout twice a week. Now I’m at a point where I’m working out three days a week. I can’t add the third day in because it’s set for twice a week. And if I go in and update the habit to three days a week, it’s going to erase all of the previous times I’ve completed the habit and start over from zero. This is super annoying and seems like something that could be easily fixed on their end. 

2. I can’t retroactively add days I’ve completed something once I create a new habit. Let’s say I decide today that I want to start tracking my workouts. So I create the habit today. Well, I worked out yesterday and the day before. But I can’t input those, because I just created the habit today. Also seems like an easy fix. 

If they fixed these two things, I would rate it five stars.

title: Good at tracking, bad at measuring
body:
I was looking for something to track my habits which is distinct from having a todo list or planning a day hour by hour. This app perfectly fits that paradigm.

UX is amazing. In some ways I found myself preferring how the app does things over my own methods. I like thinking of habits in terms of time of day, although you don’t have to label them as such.

Another nice thing is that habits can be measured with different metrics, for example, walking can be measured in miles, studying measured in time, making your bed is a single instance, etc. But this is also where I ran into problems.

Some of their default habits mandate a particular type of metric which you can’t change, so I had to create my own version.

Time-based habits have a timer you can run, which is great, except that you *must* run the timer in order for it to count; you can’t manually input time spent.

Even worse is that the timer doesn’t run unless the screen is on and the app is running. Great idea, but its execution renders the whole feature worthless. I have to track my time externally. That’s not good for an app that effectively mandates a paid subscription.

This app’s free features are so laughably limited that using it without a subscription is completely impractical. If they want to essentially force people to pay for a subscription (in not so many words) then it needs to be flawless, and it isn’t.

The app as a whole is good, but definitely run the free trial before committing.

title: Latest update has terrible UX
body:

Old review:
I agree with some other reviews I’ve seen: this was an update for the sake of updating. It has “fixed” things that were not broken to begin with. The UI used to be minimal and easy to use day to day, but now forces its paradigm of time-of-day habits. Sure, I have some habits for the evening, but a lot of anyone’s habits aren’t strictly for one time of day. It is more difficult now to just get this app to show me what I want—a simple list of my habits for the day. All day habits are now all the way to the left, the app has unneeded animations for what it is (essentially just a simple to do list style app), and the bottom bar UI now centers on adding a new habit, which is one of the actions I’ve used the least. This is making me regret subscribing to this. Maybe I can find a different app that is just simple and elegant, and doesn’t get in my way.

title: Slick UI, Little Substance
body:
Everything looks great in the UI, but it actually doesn’t functionally behave like a goal tracker. 

For example, here’s how I would track “learning algebra” through the UI description provided by Productive

“I want to have 8 reps of studying algebra repeated every week as often as once every week” 

Now in actually tracking that goal on day 1 I enter in I’ve done two reps for learning algebra. (In my case these correspond to pomodoros). Now day 2 comes around and I want to track more Algebra. That goal has been removed by Productive. I can’t input any additional Algebra studying on day 2. Why? Because Productive makes bad assumptions about how you’re using the app, highly constricted to its views about what goal tracking is. So if you didn’t get all the reps for algebra in on Day 1 well you just have to wait another week. Bruh..

So for as pretty as this app is, don’t expect anything more than a elevated to-do list. Don’t buy this.
author: Adam Smoove

title: Free version is unusable
body:
This app bills itself as a free app with optional in-app purchases, but that’s a complete misrepresentation. The app is almost unusable without a subscription. It’s a complete money grab. Literally every time you navigate away from it or change screens, it directs you to pay for a subscription. 

The subscription page that pops up every five seconds is set up in a misleading way that indicates a “free trial” (that auto-subscribes you for a full year’s price) is the only option to continue using the app for free. You can X out of the subscription page in the top left corner without agreeing to the trial, but people who aren’t tech literate won’t realize that.

I downloaded the app because my mother wanted to use it but couldn’t get it to work. As soon as I saw the subscription page, I asked my mother if she’d known she could skip it without starting a trial, and she told me no, she’d hit the obvious yellow button that said “free trial” instead. I helped her cancel her subscription and delete the app. There are much more functional free productivity apps out there that run on ads without tricking people into thinking they need a recurring subscription to use them.

title: Great UI but buggy (updated: might be iOS issue)
body:
It’s pretty intuitive at first, but when you get deeper into customization, you run into oddities and bugs. For example, it seems to be pretty aggressive about resetting streaks when you make edits to habits (understandable, but the rules around this could be more clear). You edit a habit name, and it reorders it. Sometimes things don’t get saved. Sometimes they get reordered at seemingly unpredictable times. 

And worse, I’ve only just fully set up a bunch of habits, and all of a sudden my Today shows up blank, rendering the app useless because I can’t actually see or complete the habits I spent so much time setting up. It worked well when it was working, but I am less than a month into using Productive and now it’s broken.

Update: Rebooting my iOS device seemed to fix the issue so I just raised my original rating to 4. I also had noticed another app having issues (Alarmy wasn’t showing an alarm going off), so I’m tentatively chalking at least the major issue above to an iOS problem and not a Productive one. Will report back if other issues persist or not.

title: Works well, but expensive
body:
First off, I hate hate HATE that this is a subscription based app, and doesn’t just use a one-time payment. And the monthly cost is relatively high as well.

The functionality of the app isn’t bad, but the price is completely unjustified. Since using it, I’ve found other apps under the Productivity category that do everything this app does and more, and only charge a one-time payment that is even less than this app charges per month.

The free use of this app is just an illusion as well.
First off, the app REQUIRES you to subscribe to start using it. You can choose a 1-week free trial as your subscription and then cancel it, but the actual free version at that point is so stripped of features that there’s no longer any point to it.
Second, if you don’t cancel the free trial before the week is up, either because you forget about it or just don’t mind paying to try it another month, it automatically charges you for a FULL YEAR.
No where in the app does it tell you that it defaults to charging you for an entire year in advance once the trial is up. The only way you can find out is either by getting charged, or seeing your subscription price when you go into your device subscriptions list to cancel it.

I’d bet this app makes most of its money by underhandedly charging people for a year in advance once their trial runs out. As far as I know, that isn’t even something that can be refunded which makes it all the more malicious.

Just use one of the many superior and reasonably priced apps instead, which aren’t run by sociopaths.

title: Save Your Money with the Due App
body:
Pretty disappointed after 2-3 days of using this app, I was less likely to do the tasks I set out to do because the notification system was so weak. I was hoping for an app that would make me more likely to do things like reading or journaling, and this app just wasn’t useful.

I recently paid $6.99 or so for the “Due” app, a one time charge for a persistent reminder app, while it doesn’t track my “streaks”, I can go back and look at my completed tasks.

For this app to be worth $30+ a year, there have to be more features than setting a notification, and tracking the frequency of completion. I’m frustrated that I could select a date for which I wanted a particular habit to begin-for example, putting $ into my savings account after my paycheck is deposited. Setting that habit alert to begin on my next pay day makes a lot more sense than just setting it as a biweekly goal with no set date to remind me. This goal gets lost in the shuffle.

If there were more meaningful, specific notifications that didn’t need to be set up separately as an add on option in the additional settings, I’d be more likely to use this app. If this app allowed me to snooze/reschedule, or just had more cool features, I might consider paying $12 a year, but no way would I ever pay $29.99 for a glorified reminder app.

title: Good and Bad
body:
I have a love/hate relationship with his app. I’ve used it for years and it has helped me to build some great habits. When the app works, it’s the best tool out there. I’m not a fan of subscription models, but thankfully I got in early enough so that my premium purchase carried over, which is much appreciated. 

The problem is that this app often fails to work properly. Over the last few years of use, there have been numerous stretches where the notifications and reminders simply stop working after an update. A habit app that doesn’t remind you of your goals is simply useless. I have contacted the developer a few times with the same response: “we are aware and working on a fix.” I appreciate that, but when the same issues reappear constantly, there’s something wrong with the development process. 

I wish this app were better. I want it to be better. But sadly, it’s mediocre at best.

title: Poor Syncing
body:
I love the look and general functionality of the “Productive” app, but the syncing from one mobile device to another is extremely slow. Make a change on my iPhone and it might take an hour or more for the change to appear on my iPad Pro with the devices sitting next to each other. The reverse is also true. 

Quitting and then re-opening the app multiple times on each device appears to help but obviously that’s a hassle and shouldn’t be necessary. At the same moment, my “Things 3” app will do that syncing right before my eyes (in 10 seconds or less).

I emailed Apalon support and their response was to describe the requirements for syncing which I had met from the beginning. Nothing was said about knowing they have an issue, implying that it is was just me, which I doubt. I recently retired from 25 years in hi-tech and was a teacher at Apple for more than 8, so I generally know what I’m doing with apps and devices. 

Mobile app syncing delays of over an hour are unacceptable in 2020. Support team, please respond to this review and tell users whether this issue is being addressed. I’ll give you 5 star ratings and high praise when you fix the syncing. Thank you!

Update on 5/4/2020: Received a reply from the developer (Apalon) today, but it’s likely just a form letter. Nothing said about my specific concern. Just a general statement that the company is sorry for the inconvenience, and that they are always trying to improve their app. On the bright side, at least I got a reply even if it’s from a computer rather than a real person. Ah, the world we live in these days.

title: Great concept, a little glitchy
body:
Second Edit: The app crashed until I uninstalled it and reinstalled. Best guess it that I had it passcode enabled and that wired to Face ID. Don’t do that. In fact, it hasn’t misbehaved at all since removing the passcode. Some horrible person might see my habits, but at least *I* can see them. 

Original review:

I’ve been using this for a couple of days, which is plenty of time to get the gist: the concept is clear and very well implemented. The somewhat cartoonish UI works for me—I find that the visuals give a pleasing sense of space to the UI and make it seem friendly—but you may find it, well, cartoonish. If you can’t abide it, turn on “minimalist interface” in settings. It’s perfectly functional and still attractive. 

It can nag you mercilessly if you want it to, or it can be quieter. It accommodates one-off tasks seamlessly. For the timing of habits, dividing the day into morning, afternoon, evening, and all day is simple and reflects how we experience our days. You can also time the bejeezus out of your tasks, giving them multiple timers and target occurrences—a “goal” in their nomenclature. Being able to pause tasks is welcome and also reflects facts on the ground. The canned quick-start tasks are thoughtful and meaningfully organized. All good. 

The app has also been glitchy, both on an iPhone and an iPad. Occasionally it hangs on the loading screen; once in a while it elects not to display the list of habits, although it correctly counts them as you scroll horizontally through the parts of the day.  Not deal breakers, but curious behavior for  an app running on modern hardware.

And syncing appears to poll at a leisurely pace, so updates may take a while to propagate across devices.

title: Developers Begging to Buy
body:
I have maybe written 2 reviews in nearly 12 years of using the App Store. They were positive. This is negative. When you open the app they spam you to buy. Close the prompt. Try it out first, before I buy, like we all do. Second pop up to purchase with a count down timer for a “deal.” Close it. Click a few more buttons. Another purchase prompt. Close. Another. Close it. Pick it up the next day. Pop up to buy. Close. Another and another and another and another and another. 

Let me be clear, the app seems WONDERFUL. I would gladly buy it. Worth $15-30 a year? YES! But this begging. I’ve never seen anything like it. I suppose they do it because it works. That’s sad. At this point, I wouldn’t buy it for .05 cents just on principle. *if your app is good people will buy it; if you must spam and beg at this level adherence to stick with it must be low*

title: Helping my life
body:
As someone who with ADD, a tool like this is super important.   Building routines and habits gives me some effectiveness, and this app helps me do that.  

I would like to see these enhancements:

   1.  An “at a glance view” of the entire month where you can see all the habits you have scheduled.  My therapist likes to see a summary of what I’m doing and when and I feel a quick zoom out of the entire month would help here.  

2.  The export feature is not working.  I get some Json structure but it’s all blank.  Would be fun to integrate the data on my own personal apps or other apps 

3.  Custom name tags assigned to the colors (like Trello has).  An important use case for that would be assigning the different role categories to the habits you create.  Roles of your life, for example “Husband, Father, Manager,  Personal”.  As explained in “The 7 Habits of Highly Effective  People”, categorizing your tasks this way helps make sure you keep appropriate balance in the different offices of your life.  Sure you can keep track of that mentally by different colors.  But naming those those colors gives nice explicit reinforcement.

4.  More icons for the habits.  (Current ones a great though)

title: Good idea, buggy implementation, annoying “resets”
body:
I downloaded the app earlier in January, and really liked it on my iPhone so I ended up buying the annual subscription to get the extra features.

I really like how it keeps track of my habits and reminds me to do stuff, but I find it very inflexible in terms of changing your habits as you go (which I would think is a very valid use case).

Say, for example, you start with do something x times a week; after a while, you may want to do that more frequently.

The app lets you change that, but then seems to delete all the previous entries (with a non-so-specific prompt because it tells you it will “update the stats”, not that it will “delete the stats”), which is pretty infuriating.
I would rather it resets the stats but keeps the entries if it cannot handle different stats for different periods of time (based on goal changes).

Outside of the resetting-habits issue, there is another issue which makes it a bit more annoying to use: the app never syncs with my other devices (iPad) through iCloud, even though the setting is supposedly “on”, on both iPad and iPhone, tried to enable/disable a few times to no avail, and email support wasn’t that helpful in telling me to try things they have in the FAQ section which I’ve already tried before contacting them.

Especially considering this is a paid app (can’t really think that most people can effectively use the free version), I would expect some higher quality there.

title: Sad Fall from Grace
body:
I ditto the recent reviews about all the problems. It’s sad because this use to be the undisputed best app for habits...
I don’t know if there’s a new developer or what, but I’ve never seen an app go from quality to crap so quickly. 

They keep adding beautiful design and wonderful features without testing it  out at all. Every update something new breaks, and it’s finally surpassed the annoying phase and entered the completely non-functional phase. 

This app is essentially like using... a Ferrari without an engine... a computer without a CPU... a bike without wheels... etc. 

They have had 5 separate updates since the 2.0 bug-filled design refresh, and every single time something different breaks: 

- First, the streaks were lost. I said fine, at least I can still check off habits daily.
- Next, the apple watch app stopped working. I said fine, at least I can still use the phone app.
- Then the app slowed down to the point where I had to wait 45 seconds to check off a habit. I said whatever, I already paid for it, might as well use it.
- Now, all my habits are paused and cannot be resumed no matter what I do. I literally CANNOT USE BASIC FUNCTIONALITY of the app. 

I even emailed offering to be a beta tester, and was given a generic reply that didn't address my specific email. 

Apalon should offer some reward/compensation to their paying subscribers for sticking with them through this 4 month fiasco. 

I like many others really loved this app, and perhaps I've been naive to ignore all the missteps. But it's finally dawned on me... I'm paying for a premium product that malfunctions more than any free app on my phone. 

I already emailed them numerous times about issues and I recently paid for an extra year. I don't know what else to do :(

body:

I’ve been using the premium app for about seven months and there have already been at least three times when I’ve had to resort to paper tracking to keep up my habits.

To the development team: date math is hard. You need a quality assurance team. Do unit tests and beta testing. Don’t be in such a rush to push new features out the door. In order to make habits stick, your users need stability. The updates released in the last seven months that broke things have all because you’ve been too hasty to push out an unnecessary feature.

I am canceling my subscription.

title: Do NOT trust this app for long term goals
body: If you want an app that you can trust with your personal growth, this is not the app. I used this app to track some very personal and meaningful growth, with over 820 days (that's over 2 years!) of perfect days. I succeeded in meeting my goals Every. Single. Day. for more than two years. What happened? Apalon made an update and wiped my data. I'm now back at zero. I'm devastated. My stomach is in my throat. Do not make the mistake I did in trusting them with your goals. Do not trust them to track your progress. Use Google calendar, or a physical journal, or anything else. Do not trust them long term. It might work today, or day 800, but eventually you will wake up and find your progress gone and with it your sense of accomplishment! Note: I did reach out to support. They replied after a day, saying "We're working on it." From there I didn't hear from them. I have emailed them two more times, without a word back, which was over a week ago. I'm beyond heartbroken. Again, do not trust this app for any of your long term goals, you will regret it. Eventually they will destroy your data.

title: Used to be good app
body:
Update(19-feb) : 
It’s been three weeks since the sorting habits is broken . After spending a long valuable time sorting the habits , it’s really unacceptable to see them go back to random order again . How long will it take it fix issues which were once working fine ? 

Original review :
I am a paid member of the app for a few
Months now and been a regular user . The app used to be simple and very useful , where you can create new habits and sort it with ease,  I used as my reference to get an idea of how my day must be sequenced.  . A recent update completely broke the sorting functionality and completely jumbled up all the habits that I had kept sorted until now . I contacted support and reported this . I got a response on how to fix it again . I spent 30 mins  to sort all the habits manually once again as it was broken by the update. But once I went to another screen in the app and back , the sorting went away again and it’s all jumbled up again  . This is Extremely careless of them especially for something people pay lots of  money for.  

Another clear indicator of their carelessness is when you go read their version history - none of them describe what the actual changes in the new version is . They copy paste the same genetic description  for every version .

Updated:

Tried twice more to reorder my habits , and it again went back to jumbled state . I have spent 1 hr so far just to sort the habits but giving up

title: Not worth the $$
body:
At first i was excited to use this app. It seemed exactly what i was looking for. A task management app that would operate daily to keep me on my toes when needed. If you’re considering this app, let me break it down:

Consistency: If you are going to be actively on it, daily, and i mean daily.. then this may be for you. It’s an app that organizes reminders (basically). When you’re active on the app, then it will be active with their reminders too.  If you’re not active, unfortunately, the reminders are inconsistent. Sometimes they’re often, sometimes they’re not. If you’re someone who forgets to do something, for literally a day, then forget it. The moment you stop, This app will NOT follow up and hold you accountable to your tasks. You will end up going days without using the app. A waste of money. 

If you like analytics, you can see your performance overtime. I like that. However, still a 4 star app at most. 

Overall, this is Something you can save $$ by doing it yourself in your phone. Set your own reminders in your phone with alarms and that will be more consistent then this app. At the end of the day, i would prefer to have my money back then use the app. This may be for some, but for me, it’s a hard NO right now. 

Good luck and Enjoy!

title: Great focused tool, one minor gripe: surface the Notes, please
body:
I have been using Productive for about 2 years and I find its focus on repeating habits generallywell thought out. I use it most days for key reminders. The interface is clear and easy to use. I think for the vast majority of people looking for a habit tracker, it’s great. 

The one minor criticism is that in a recent update, the Notes field has gotten buried in the interface and I have to work consciously to find it. 

I might be an edge case, but I use the Notes field for several of my habits to review key aspects of the habit. For example, I keep a daily habit of reviewing people in my life who have some sort of challenge: I want to see their name and their challenge so I can decide if I need to check in or do something. 

To get to the Notes field now I have to make 3 presses: 

1. Click on the Habit detail (>).
2. I have to look around the details page, see nothing that looks like a note, and remember to click on the ellipsis (...) on the upper right of the screen.
3. Click the Notes icon. 

That’s 3 clicks and several seconds of having to remember where to look for the notes. I wish the Notes were surfaced more easily, such as 

One other minor observation: when I have a Notes field visible, the new interface with the big blue + symbol obscures the last line or two of the notes: I have to physically drag the note upward to be able to see the last two lines, then they spring back below the blue + symbol. This seems intrusive and counter-productive to me: if I open the notes, I want to see the notes. 

I think if the Notes interface issues I outline above were fixed, I’d give this application 5 stars.

Thanks.

title: Best purchase I’ve made on the AppStore.
body:
This app succeeds where physical, paper planners fail. Over the last 15 years or so I’ve bought many planners and notebooks geared towards tracking goals and staying on task, and I’d use them for a few months (if that) and they’d get retired to a desk drawer to be forgotten. I’ve decided the reason these fail me, or I fail them, is because they are so tedious. This app takes the tedious work out of the equation.

My favorite things about it:

The repeating of tasks.

I can make tasks repeat on specific days or  x amount of times per week or even biweekly.
Reminders and timers.

I can set several reminders and even a duration.
Tracking progress motivates me. (Really, it’s the best.)

A habit I track is “No soda today!” I have that set for evening daily and if I made it the day with no soda, I mark it as done. It tracks all my successful days. But if I have one, I skip it, it breaks the streak, and here’s the thing: in the past this would have really de-motivated me to cut back, but with this I see right there that I was able to go however many days, which doesn’t allow me to forget my success and I know I can do it again, and I want to. I love love love that. 
The design/interface.

The colors are nice, the style is minimal, you aren’t overwhelmed with text and nothing is an eyesore. 
Siri Compatibility.

What I would like to change/see added:

Categories.

Ability to create categories to assign habits to if I want, and a page to view just those categories. It would allow us to isolate just Exercise, or just Skin Care, etc. That would help me a lot. 

Overall, I think this app is great in every way. The yearly premium price of $30 is consistent with the cost of the cute planners on Etsy, only those pale in comparison to the abilities, ease, and potential of the app. It’s a great value and I highly recommend it.

title: update regrets.
body:
I had LOVED this app from day one. I began using it not long after the release years ago. This evening I updated the app and am extremely upset about the changes. 

• The format is very different. I don’t know how to best describe it. One word would be complicated. Another is perplexing; why is there a sloth (?), trees, a sun, birds, a moon, ... ? Why did they get rid of the minimalistic list on a single ‘page’? The format is mind-blowing (and not in a positive way). 
• I can no longer find the setting that gives me the option which background color I want. Now, it is dark grey/black by default. I hope I am missing something. And because of the grey background, my icons can no longer be grey. 
• I reset all of my stats to zero yet the app displays that I’ve had 27 perfect days from January 1-31, 2020. Today is January 1, 2020. I have not marked a single habit as complete and I have not traveled to the future and back.
• All of my weekly habits are not displaying as they did before. Some are simply not there. Yet they are listed in the habit menu. 

There are other things ticking me off but I’m simply too frustrated to continue. I am devastated by what they’ve done to this app. This use to be my favorite app and I told many people about it. As of now, I’m doubtful I will continue using it and it breaks my heart.

title: Please untorpedo the interface
body:
Thank you for fixing the weekly habits bug. I got my streak back.

The minimalist interface option is a nice thought, and I appreciate it, but it doesn’t actually fix the problem. The sloth isn’t the issue. I like the sloth, it’s adorable. It’s not the sloth that makes the interface unnecessarily complicated, it’s the layout.

I don’t reliably check in with this app during every section of every day. I don’t have time for that. I check in the morning to see what my day looks like and in the evening to make sure I marked everything I did. I always need to see my full day schedule and I never need to see separate pages for afternoons and stuff. It keeps opening into the morning section instead of the full day, giving me an incorrect idea of what my day needs to look like.

Your product description suggests this app may be helpful to adults with adhd. Please think about what that user experience might be like for a user with attention and focus issues. You open the app, you see what looks like your full day schedule. You forget to check whether it’s actually your morning schedule instead. You think you have your day sorted. You happen to open the app in the late afternoon. You’re now panicking because you to-do list is not what you thought it was. Swiping around through a day is a huge extra step, and it’s pretty disorienting.

It’s a shame because the simplicity of the interface was what set this app apart from the competition. It’s why it was my top recommendation for habit tracking apps.

I’d really love to see a minimalist interface that’s actually minimalist as an interface instead of the same overly complicated multipart swipe mess but without the art. I liked the art. I want a minimalist option with only a daily list and none of this swiping around to get to it, or the horrible possibility of accidentally swiping off of it into a different view without noticing.

I’d rather like to keep the sloth though if it’s all the same. It’s really adorable.

Downloaded this app to try it but its UI is terrible for those who just want to try. Its Try for free banners are complete lies bringing you to a purchase immediately screen. Want a reminder or to try the super basics of this app even for a week? No go. It even bugged during the tutorial and I had to force quit the app when it wanted me to complete a task that was not even there. Bad experience through and through.

Responding to the developers response... There is no free trial. The banner says free trial but when tapped it wants to start the paid subscription immediately. It does not offer the usually 1 week free and then if not canceled it will charge for the subscription as was advertised on the banner.

title: Pretty helpful, kind of frustrating at times
body:
So, overall I like the app and will continue using it.  There’s just a few quirks that kind of irritate me at times. 

1) The display and graphics are just a little too “cute” for my taste.  I find that all the encouraging phrases, sunrise diagrams and rainbows are distracting from the point of the app.  It’s supposed to help you accomplish habits...I don’t want any frills to get in the way.  

2) The second issue is that if you change anything about a habit, you lose all stats on it.  So for example, if you have a habit that used to be “anytime” and you want to change it to an “evening” habit, you lose all previous completion stats.  Why is that?  It makes it feel like you can’t really edit habits, you’re actually just deleting it and starting new because you now have no stats to look back on, which is honestly pretty discouraging.  

So yeah, it’s a helpful app and I’ll probably keep using it, but if I come across something better that’s more professional looking and allows for more customization, I’ll probably switch over.

title: Version 2.0. Not so good
body:
12/20/2019: Well, the developers released a whole new layout for this app, and in doing so kinda ruined it. Now I have this useless sun and moon graphic at the top of the screen, which is pretty much a waste of space. Additionally, I now have four lists to manage and have to keep sliding left and right between them. Completely useless. 

But there is more. Lots of the menu options don’t work, and...  when you upgrade you’re existing habits will not all display correctly. Say bye bye to any streaks you had. If you really need your data for anything important, you’ll want to get it out of this app. 

While I’m always open to improvements and change, this app has taken a step backwards when it comes to appearance and usability. It’s unfortunate. Between the new layout and the apps continuously occurring bugs, like a few with every release, I cannot recommend this app any longer. 🙁

————————————————————

11/12/2019 Update: DO NOT TURN ON PASSCODE LOCK, it causes the app to crash at startup. Customer service was responsive to my emails for help, but ultimately I fixed the startup problem myself. Deleted the app and reinstalled. After reinstall, all my data was gone, but after leaving the app open for a few minutes, it synced to iCloud and everything was back. Note, I had iCloud sync turned on prior to app breaking, so my data was already in the cloud. 3 stars as this issue really shouldn’t have happened to begin with. Again, turning on passcode lock caused the app to crash startup, the don’t turn it on. 

11/09/2019: Well, the latest update has rendered this app unusable. It crashes at start up every time on iOS12. Useless...

title: Train Wreck
body:
This app was fantastic, and a cornerstone of my life. After all, I use it to organize my day every day.

And then something happened. They released a new version: a slow motion, unending train wreck beyond imagination. They apparently did no testing whatsoever before unleashing the new version on its unsuspecting users.

One of the key features what is the ability to put the habits in order. For example, you might 1) get dressed, then 2) go to work. The ability to sort habits is broken, this is a known defect, and this defect renders the app useless. If for example, my daily plan starts with 1) go to sleep, then 2) clear email, that makes no sense.

But the worst defect is when it started deleting all my daily habits. I put a lot of time and care into designing these: The name, icon, color, and daily order.

Then all my habits suddenly vanished. Not only did I lose a valuable tool that was the cornerstone of my day, but I had to go through that work all over again. I added my habits to the app again, and they disappeared again.

Again, this is a known defect. Their tech-support is prompt, and any problem they will reply to you and tell you “we are aware of the problem and we are working on it.” 

But that doesn’t help, and the problems persist. It might be OK to release an app for buying wine, or editing selfies, that has bugs. But when your app is called productive, and I’m assuming for example used by people in business, it is inexcusable to release such a buggy app.

I finally gave up and deleted the app. I might try it again -Cautiously - say in six months, when they have gotten their act together, and actually bother to test out the app before they unleash it on their users.

My only complaint is that several months ago they added the feature to see what tasks are due tomorrow, but those tasks cannot be completed until tomorrow. While this makes some sense, the app has no problem letting you complete tasks after the day they were due. I like this feature and use it to catch up when I fall behind, but I hate that I can’t get even a day ahead when I know I have a busy stretch coming up. title: It was my go-to for years! Until...
body: I’ve had this app since 2016. It really helped me get back on my feet during a difficult time, so to me, it was a game changer. It was one of my most reliable apps, but alas it has one major flaw that made me look elsewhere for a habit tracker 4 years later. Recently I got an iPad and two Apple Watches, and the syncing between devices just wasn’t smooth at all. Sometimes it didn’t happen altogether. The iPad was left out most of the time, and when that happened, it usually ended in habits being duplicated on all the devices. It also took some effort to get it to sync when I switched watches in the morning - on the watch it would say “syncing” and nothing would happen until I messed with it on my iPhone. This process would take me 10+ minutes. Overall, this is a great app if you only use it on one device, but across several devices, some major bugs still need to be fixed.

That alone helps me not to feel overwhelmed, which is a problem I have with the everyday mundane stuff I usually put off. I love how you can very simply change the order of your habits without inputting the the time they need to be done- I don't like the pressure of racing the clock for mundane stuff. title: Trap of an app
body:
I downloaded the app and deleted within an hour of messing around with the limited free trial functions. To my surprise, a week later I was charged for an entire year of the premium subscription. The developer is clearly taking advantage of fine-print subscription terms and people who value their time (might be this apps exact target audience...coincidence? I don’t think so).

If you fall for this “trap of an app” by making both the mistake of initially downloading it and forgetting to unsubscribe from automatic renewals before deleting, you will need to request a refund from Apple Support as developers don’t have control over account payments - how convenient for them.  

My request for a refund was denied immediately despite going to support the day of the charge. I also submitted an accidental subscription renewal, and have yet to hear back or see my money returned.  Until I do, or if I don’t, I won’t be using and/or trialing apps from this developer moving forward.
