title: Great Tool
body:
This app has helped me, far more than any other on the App Store, to take control of my life. It has been especially useful in creating a healthy lifestyle, and to conquer depressive habits I had never been able to. 

The accountability the app brings is one that is lacking in pressure. If you end up not being able to complete a habit, you don’t get negative feedback. Most habit forming apps on the App Store have negative feedback when you are unable to meet your goals, which can become quickly frustrating and cause more self-criticism. Other apps on the market will send an obnoxious amount of reminders, that eventually become easy to ignore. Rather the app uses as many, or as little, reminders as you want. You can choose which days of the week and what time of day the habits need completed by. With the Premium feature, you are able to create as many habits as you want and gain access to more fun settings. For me, the amount I paid for the yearly subscription was worth it for the changes I have seen in my life.

The only problems I have found is in the weekly section. You don’t get the option of choosing the day of the week for habits in the weekly tab. I have a plant I water every two weeks, always on Saturday’s, but there is currently no way to specify this option. Because I can find no other problems, and because of the personal help this app has provided, I am giving it 5 stars.

title: Now only 3 habits for free. Down from 5.
body:
So I don’t normally write reviews but I thought I would mention something about this app because of how unusable it is in the free version. I see a review from Jun 24th of this year that complains that you could only make 5 free habits in the free version of this app. Apparently in the months since then this company thought that was too generous and have now lowered that to 3 habits total. 

While they can totally do that within their rights, everything about this app screams money hungry. Going from 5 to 3 habits is one. The other is that they deceptively try and sign you up for a subscription by saying that it’s free. They also prompt you to subscribe every 3-4 screens. They also limited LIGHT MODE to a paid feature. Are you serious? 

I’m an iOS developer and I know exactly how little effort it takes to build light mode and dark mode into an app. The design is nice but the features are not worth nearly what they’re asking for it.

Eventually they will make it so that you can open this app make 1 goal and then they’ll only show you the subscription screen. They would be so much better off if they just charged once to everyone for a lite version of the app (say 10 habits) and then premium subscribers get unlimited habits. This is not a $15 per year app (the 50% discount they offer everyone). Please do yourselves a favor and don’t try and nickel and dime your users. It’s just super distasteful and makes people upset.

I understand that subscriptions are a much more stable business model and that they’re the way that Apple is suggesting apps go. I also understand that the work that has gone into making this app look and feel clean and crisp is harder than some may assume. It’s difficult to design simply. Unfortunately this app doesn’t get to shine like it could because of the business decisions for marketing it.

title: Helps establish new routines
body: This app is very helpful with establishing and tracking new routines. I enjoy the color scheme, and the ease of swiping a task right or left to indicate if it has been completed or skipped for good reason (such as being out of town). I included some basic things that I’m already good at doing (taking vitamins and medication every day) so that I will always have something to mark as completed, in order to give me momentum, and to stack my habits. From what I can tell, the highest frequency you can track is 3 times a day. If you want to track number of ounces of water you drank, or how many times you did something else, I don’t see a way to do that. The Tally app would be better for that. Also, I like the any.do app for tracking and scheduling one-time tasks, including projects with multiple subtasks. For making and tracking big goals, Strides might be the app for you. Having recently entered a new phase of life, this app, Productive, is my app of choice for creating and tracking good habits and routines.

title: Getting worse with every “update”
body:
I’ve been using this app since the “premium” version was a one-time optional payment. It was simple, clean, and did the job of counting how many times I completed a given task. Lately, it’s been degrading harshly as the developers try to add silly bells and whistles. 

- Items I have scheduled to do X days per week “break” their streak every Sunday.
- Two items duplicated themselves for no reason. 
- All day today, since updating the app, “Today” has been tomorrow and everything I’ve yet to do today is marked as missed. 

Stop adding pointless “improvements” to an app that worked just fine before - you’re breaking it. I want my streaks to carry over week to week more than I want an annoying “way to go” pop-up every 50 item completions.

UPDATE: I just changed how many times I wanted to do something in a week (which I do frequently with some items for my own reasons) and ALL my previous data for that task (HUNDREDS of completions) has been erased!! What are you doing?!

UPDATE 2: Just had a reminder chime (at 23:30) for a task for which I never set a reminder. And there’s no way to delete it! You’ve completely broken what used to be a fine app. At this point, the only reason I haven’t given up on you is the hundreds- and thousands-long streaks of which I’d like to keep a record.

I accidentally deleted a completed task from yesterday and had no way of reinstating it. You can only have a limited number of tasks without paying. The to do list function is pretty similar to Wunderlist but with stats on how often you stick to your habits, which I don’t really care about enough to pay for. Every other click on the app leads to a pop up to in app purchases which is really annoying. I’d rather sit through a 30 second ad twice a day than pay for this or continue to use it and deal with the constant pop ups. Maybe I’d pay a onetime nominal fee to use this but not a monthly charge.
author: hja91

title: Just wait for iOS 13 Reminders update.
body:
The app functions properly, as in its not glitchy or broken, but this is like a Palm-Pilot-era reminders app, with no in-depth features or capability. It’s basically Apple’s Reminders with the ability to see how many times you’ve completed each task on a calendar. It’s absolutely not worth the deceptively high subscription fees. (I say deceptive because they threw 3 different prices for the same thing at me within 2 minutes of opening the app). It doesn’t even have simple features like proper cross-device syncing or a library of tasks to choose from. That’s right, you have to create every task completely from scratch, just like Apple’s Reminders, just like a PDA from 2003, down to manually choosing things like background colors and icons pulled from some free to use clip art gallery. 

I would have just deleted it and moved on but they have some sleazy hoops to jump through when you open it for the first time that aim to trick you into signing up for a “free trial” that auto-renews a week later for $30. If you don’t fall for it then they throw another screen at you offering the same thing for $15 (but only if you take the deal within 59 minutes, lol). They even put a countdown clock ON THE HOME SCREEN of the app after that like those awful Clash of Clans type games 🙄

So yeah, those practices rubbed me the wrong way so I felt inclined to leave this completely honest review about what this app is and isn’t. 

Bottom line, if you’re interested in paying a premium price for a full featured and innovative productivity app then there are MUCH better options available. Better yet, just wait a couple weeks and use the improved version of Reminders in iOS 13.

title: Really annoyed 🙄
body: Ugh is all I can say for this app. I downloaded this thinking it was going to change my life and make me a better person. But unfortunately, the only lives changing here are the ones of people that pay the app for more habits. I could only create like three or four habits until it reached the limit. That really annoyed me, and it's the reason I gave this app one star. But to be honest with myself and the developers, without the habit limit, I probably would have given this app five stars. This app really has a lot of potential, and I have nothing against the developers, it's just that this app didn't live up to its potential. First up, you all know my good friend the habit limit, the layout also is one of my worst enemies, I hate simple layouts, even though I know most people love them, and I'm not quite satisfied with the way the icons work, maybe instead of icons, you could maybe have a drop down box with topics like "Workout" or "Around the house" on it, and it would immediately add an icon to the side of a habit, it would just be easier than looking through each icon and seeing which one corresponds with a specific habit. One more thing I need to complain about, who needs a to-do list app anyway? The only thing u might need it for is the notifications. But u could literally just take a pad and paper and be done with it! Like seriously! But there is one good thing we can salvage from this wreck of an app, and it's the coloring. I know, so LOOOWWW, but I love the black background and the standard colors, I might not love simple layouts, but I love simple colors. That's all I have to say for this app, and I wouldn't recommend it for someone who isn't willing to spend money on something you could do on a pad and paper. Sorry, but this app could have been so much better, but it didn't live up to the expectations I had for it.

title: Deceptive Pricing
body:
Developer not honest about the price. The actual price, a $33.00/yr subscription - which you’re only told about upon downloading and starting the app- is way too high for this app.

UPDATE: as a business, when you are accused of wrongdoing or dishonest business practices - specifically deceptive pricing - the appropriate response is NOT to reply by stating the obvious ( i.e., “It is up to you to decide whether or not you want to get a subscription”...obviously it’s up to me, it’s my money) and ignore the consumer’s actual complaint or invite the consumer to purchase your other products (i.e., “You can always check out our other apps”...why would I want to purchase something else from the very same company that I just accused of wrongdoing or dishonest business practices??)  I’d appreciate it if you address the actual complaint of deliberately deceptive pricing - of which you have been accused several times by reviewers in the reviewer feedback. You can correct the situation by changing your dishonest practice of deceptive pricing - not by offering the user a canned, deliberately disingenuous response.

title: Buggy, buggy, and oh yeah, BUGGY!!!
body:
I downloaded this app and paid for a year subscription based on all the neat feature and thousands of positive reviews. After hours of setup and fine tuning of my habits I began to use it and thought it was pretty good. 

But then I tried to use the timer function for a habit. I had set the timer for a habit to 40 minutes and turned it on, and about m hour later I went in to check how much time was left since it felt like it had been too long. Turns out the timer doesn’t work it you leave the app or lock your phone. It just stops and then picks back up when you open the app again. I submitted feedback and was told they would consider adding the feature at some point. Why even bother in the first place guys?

Then as I used the app more and more, I found my habits were starting to show up randomly as “Overdue,” even though ALL previous days habits were marked “Done,” or “Skipped.” So I reset the stats and started over. Then it happened again, and then again this morning. 

You can’t be productive, with Productive, because you will spend all your time trying to figure out why the app is behaving erratically. Year subscription? Guess I’ll chalk it up to a learning experience, delete the app and go back to Reminders, which is getting an overhaul in iOS 13 anyway. Enjoy the $30 guys, you won’t get another dime from me ever.

title: Misleading
body: I thought it was a GREAT app at first. It’s rare I buy a premium from the start, but I knew I would love this app. HOWEVER. I paid for ONE YEAR of premium. $14.99 on a special was supposed to get me ONE YEAR of premium. One month after buying that year of premium I was charged again. Thinking it was just a mistake I had jump through tons of hoops to get a refund. They said ok we got your refund and cancelled your subscription but you’ll still have access to the premium you paid for. Which I’m still thinking is ONE YEAR. Next time I launch the app, it says “oh no, you’re premium has expired”. When I signed up and bought the premium, it did NOT say the $14.99 was monthly. It said $14.99 for ONE YEAR. So be aware. It’s a great app. But buying the premium is very misleading and you will be charged monthly for something that said yearly. Without premium, I personally don’t find the app worth it and I’m not paying $14.99 a month for it. That’s more than Netflix. So I will be finding another app.

title: I hope I don’t get charged.
body: Downloaded app before looking at the reviews. After hitting continue it prompted me to either pay or subscribe and start a free trial. I did not subscribe, as I do not want to get charged at a later date, as I do not want to pay for this app. I noticed on the screen that was asking me subscribe for the free trial and pay there was an X on the top of that page. So I exited out of the page asking me to subscribe. And again, I did not subscribe or give any consent to start a free trial! I simply exited the alert asking me to subscribe and start a free trial, as again I DO NOT WANT TO SUBSCRIBE OR START A FREE TRIAL I DO NOT WANT TO PAY FOR THIS APP OR BE CONNECTED TO IT. So I exited out of that page. This is when it gets weird. After I exited that page it asks if I want to turn on notifications for the app. I did not get an option to skip or exit out of this page, and as I just exited out of subscribing or starting a free trial I thought it VERY ODD that it was asking me about notifications. So I hit continue on the notification question. Again, I have not provided any agreement to sign up for a free trial and have NOT subscribed. After I hit continue to the notification question and alert pops up that allows me to choose if I want to turn notifications on or not. I select I do not want notifications as at this point I just want to delete this app, but I first want to make sure this shady SHADY app didn’t somehow  set me up as subscribed without my consent. So after I made sure the notifications were turned off this app that I exited out of subscribing and did NOT request a free trial for, did NOT give consent or any of my personal information is now allowing me to set up tasks?!?! How is this possible when I did NOT subscribe or agree to a free trial?!?! Am I suppose to believe that this app is registering its downloaded as free trial participants and subscribing them upon downloading the app?!?! I certainly did NOT consent to that. I exited out of the question I want to delete the app. So my question is am I going to be charged for a subscription I did NOT consent to? Am I going to be charged for a subscription when asked if I wanted I deleted the screen? I truly hope I will not be charged for downloading an app, exiting out of a question about subscribing, and then selecting I don’t want notifications for an app I was trying to delete within ten seconds of downloading!

title: Working so far
body:
I’ve only had this a day, but it’s doing exactly what I want it to — which is to help me stay on task with a fairly regimented routine. I’m a mother of two children not yet in school, and my older son is enjoying having a schedule to follow. So far, so good.

UPDATE:
After one week, I’m still really liking this app. The interface is appealing and easy to use once you figure out where all the features are. The notification flags are great for keeping me on task. My days have gone much more smoothly and my kids are getting really great at knowing what to expect during the day for the past week. We have far fewer struggles and see much better behavior from them. I’m Type B when it comes to schedules — even though I thrive with one, I have a hard time staying on task by myself. I’ve done yoga every morning for a week! I’ve even had enough time to go to the gym. By myself. With two kids at home with their dad. Seriously! So glad I found this app.

title: Good
body:
This is a good app. But it is lacking a few things:
- The ability to mark something as NOT done and thus dismiss it from your list for the day (or whatever period). This is the case for those habits you’re working on of NOT doing something (i.e. quitting something), and when you fail to NOT do whatever that is. It’s not helpful that they linger in your list all day until you can’t remember for sure anymore if you did or did not do the thing.
- Habit history should not reset when you make minor tweaks to the schedule—such as changing a habit from morning to afternoon. The app should kindly handle such adjustments rather than nuking your history as though you had changed from weekends to weekdays or something so drastic.

title: My gold stars!
body:
I’ve only been using this app for about a day, so I really can’t tell you anything about its usability, or whether it has bugs, or whether it’s going to work for 6 9/10 days and then poop out on the day that you start paying, I really have no idea about any of that.

What I do like is that little kid part of me that gets triggered by an app like this, where, it’s the handheld version of being able to put that checkmark on the chalkboard or put that sticker on the board, or crossing some thing off y/our to do list...only they’re all for ME this time :-) 

So often, that to-do list, is actually a list of all the things that other people have reminded you that you need to do! Do do do do do! This app reminds me to make time on my list for small, every day, things, that I can totally let slide if I’m not careful. So I’ll hope that it lives up to the hype, I already put in my, “things I do every day“, list on the app, and there’s a few things that don’t feel completely intuitive, but I’m sure if I look at the help section or the FAQs, someone’s probably experience the same thing and will be able to help. 

And if for some reason, it doesn’t live up to the hype, there’s always the good old fashion pencil and a piece of paper.

title: (UPDATED) Poor sync, worse service ruins fantastic app for me
body:
The 6/3 “Developer Response” and private email I received are useless, so I lowered my star rating from 3-2.

I reached out via comments after many months of direct contact. I don’t know if the developers can’t or won’t solve the issue (hard to believe they can’t), but I’ve lost patience with their continued apologies, gratitude, and requests for more patience. 

I have yet to witness any  attempt to “resolve the situation.” In fact, now I’m not sure they even understand the problem as the email referred to making the sync work “faster” and “more reliably.” When something does not work AT ALL, both speed and reliability are irrelevant.

I received the private email Friday and replied immediately. The public “Developer Response” yesterday is the only info I’ve received since. Nothing is resolved. Is it even undertstood?

From the email:
“We do hope to come up with a solution that will fix the problem and improve your experience with the app!
Our team hopes for your understanding and patience.”

Nope. I’m out of patience and mostly because I sincerely do not understand.

--------------------
ORIG POST 5/30/19
I've been using Productive for a very long time--nearly three years. For the most part, I love it. When it works, it works very well. It's not nor should it be used as a task manager except for tasks that you want to become habitual. And for that, it totally works. I love getting that little rush of dopamine every time I check-off a habit or see my 96-day streak or whatever. Achieving a "perfect" day also is surprisingly not just satisfying but exciting. And I have found the recent updates to be very good too, particularly the new slider at the top to switch between the current part of the day versus the entire day.

I don't remember if the app already had the ability to sync via iCloud when I began using it, but I seem to remember it didn't. Instead, I believe it was added at some point, and I was so happy. Now, I could use Productive on both my iPhone and iPad seamlessly. And that was the case for quite a long time. And suddenly, it wasn't.

I would give Productive five stars if it wasn't for their inability to make the sync work correctly (in ways that every other app I have that syncs via iCloud appears to do seamlessly). But even worse is their piss-poor customer service around this issue. Not only have they been unable to solve/fix it, they have provided me with either damaging help or no help whatsoever.

I first encountered this problem between 6-9 months ago, I think. I contacted Apalon via their support email. On the plus side, they are very responsive; they generally replied within 24-48 hours. They suggested I make sure that iCloud sync was turned on. They suggested I delete the app from my iPad and reinstall it. Since it should be syncing to iCloud, the data will just repopulate. As the syncing had worked for a while, all the habits were listed on the iPad, but the historical data was incomplete because it wasn't receiving updates. And if I marked something complete on the iPad, it wouldn't affect the iPhone app. After deleting and reinstalling the iPad app, nothing came back. The app simply remained empty. 

Their next suggestion was to delete the iPhone app and reinstall, and again, nothing should be lost because it's syncing with my iCloud account, right? If you look at the options under "Manage iCloud," along with 'iCloud sync" are options to "Export data" and "Delete data." One might think that if you can export data, there might also be a way to later reimport that data. So I decided to export the data before deleting the app. I would say, "Good thing I did," because of course when I reinstalled the app on my iPhone, no data returned.

But then, when I contacted Apalon support again, and I told them that their suggestions hadn't worked, but I had exported my data and maybe they could tell me how to repopulate it to at least one of the apps, I received nothing more than an apology. They ignored my question about how to use the exported data. They wouldn't say it couldn't be imported. They just won't say anything. I've asked multiple times.

Eventually, I had to restart from scratch, and after doing so, the sync worked again. For a while. Until it didn't. I wrote them again, repeating what had happened before and asking about using the exported data. This time they made no suggestions. They just apologized again for the trouble and said they were looking into it and appreciated my patience. Well, that was over five months ago.

And then, suddenly, the syncing did begin to work again. For a while. And then in March, it again stopped. This time, I only deleted the iPad app, and upon reinstalling it noticed that if I added a task via the iPad app, that task WOULD sync back to the iPhone, and any changes made to THAT TASK on the iPhone would sync back to the iPad. However, any tasks that already existed on the iPhone still won't sync with the iPad, and any new tasks created on the iPhone won't populate to the iPad or sync. 

Obviously, I wrote Apalon about this again, and most recently, the response I received was as follows:

"We're deeply sorry that it takes such long time to fix the issue.

We do hope for your patience till we get this resolved.

Apologies once again and thank you for using our app."

I'm not a programmer, and I'm sure there's plenty I don't understand about what's happening under the hood. And yet, again, this is the only app that syncs via iCloud that I've ever had this kind of long-standing, unfixable issue with. And that maybe wouldn't bother me so much if Apalon would at least figure out a workaround (like, a way to reimport exported data?) or explain what's going on and why what must be a pretty basic part of Apple's developer kit is so broken on their app that they can't fix it.

It pains me to start over with a new habit app, but I think I'm finally ready to do so.

title: Game changer, or rather a habit changer
body:
To understand, I’m a 33...or is it 34...year old man who struggles with ADHD having been diagnosed in the early 90s when no one knew what ADD or ADHD was. Most still don’t, but many think they do. It’s a real condition and is hard to grasp what it’s like for most folks. But enough of that. 

I came across this app looking for a better Reminders app to help me track to-do lists and other idea lists which are scattered amongst Reminders, Keep, One Note, and Notes. I didn’t even know there were apps for “habits,” but I know I function better with structure and routine. 

As I’m getting older, and due to the stress of my career (law enf/public safety), it has gotten harder instead of easier. Some grow out of ADHD or at least the hyperactivity, but not me. I have weak coping skills compared to the additional stressors my career has induced over the years. I often hear, “Maybe this isn’t a good fit for you,” but have proven many wrong over the years. 

However, I’m struggling again and this app has been a true game changer. I only have to remember to check this app and with my wife’s old Apple Watch it has been a dream. 

I set every important thing I want done according to morning, noon, or night as well as once a week, two weeks, etc. 

By default, the app shows only the items for your current time such as morning habits. For example, waking up on time. Check. Eat breakfast, brush teeth, take meds, get dressed, walk dogs. Check—and so on. 

On Sunday evenings once a week I take the trash out. On Monday, anytime, I bring the empty can back behind the house. 

This app is great. I have a different app to keep track of To-Dos, but wish I could do that in this app as a separate feature or function. 

But for creating a routine and sticking to it for the most part...it definitely helps. I’m able to be as vague or as detailed as I want concerning my daily/weekly/monthly tasks and truly feel good checking them off. It also shows statistics on a per task/day/month basis so I can see my progress. It would take years of practice at the same routine for me to accomplish ALL of these things I add daily/weekly and never stray or forget them. 

With this app, it’s taken a week. My wife even said she’s noticed I’m a LOT more productive and she’s happier for it. 

No, this won’t solve ADHD or focusing issues. It will, however, aid in a powerful way that carrying a notepad and pen in my pocket each day (when I don’t leave it at home by accident), in a tremendous way. 

The only thing I ever have to do is one simple task: check my watch/phone. The rest of my regular day is laid out for me in a way I can do more with my time and just get things done. 

Sorry for the long review, but it’s been so effective I just had to share my experience. Feel free to use this as a testimonial. My name is Brandon by the way. And thank you!

The only reason I ever stop using this app is because I am so bad at sticking to a routine. But when I put forward the effort, this is the only app I have found that actively encourages me. title: Small price to pay
body:
If you want a habit and nothing else is working I highly recommend this app. I’ve read so many books on the psychology behind building habits and this app touches upon those same principles. Being able to make a streak is extremely rewarding and instead of doing something to achieve a reward you are competing against yourself. Being able to check something off as completed is very satisfying. The app really is best used in premium but if you’re serious about your goals then you can spare the cash. In my case, paying up the money is actually more motivating because I want to make sure I don’t waste it by ignoring my goals. 
Overall, great app. Wish you could go into more details as far as times a reminder happens but it’s a good investment in yourself.

title: Skip Justification Option?
body:
So far I am enjoying it and it is helping me with my various tasks. I would like to see though, a feature where I can make a task as ‘optional’ or something to where if I don’t do it/skip it, it wouldn’t count as a negative strike for it. Or maybe have a justification block come up to explain why I can’t do a task. For example:
I have a task to hit the gym in the morning but sometimes I can’t because I have to go into the office instead to get some work done which makes me then ‘skip’ it. But for those days I have another hit the gym task set in the afternoon just in case I can’t make the morning one. So at some point, one of those hit the gym tasks is going to be ‘skipped’ since I’ll do the other one.

Unless I’m missing a setting or setting these up completely wrong I would like to see this feature added so it doesn’t seem like I’m always skipping something.

title: really helpful
body:
The Productive app helps me to reconnect with my executive function as perimenopause destroys my sleep and gets me down. I’ve been a DIY CBT junky to stay on track and build better habits for decades, using paper lists and a shared online calendar.  My daughter recently described me as “the executive function” of the family, but I am using many new props to retain that title and the Productive app has become key. 

As the Mom of a family of 4, I support others in their meals, sleep, hw, their own CBT weekly shifting routines, Rx management, etc. Importantly, the app reminds me to do immediate things for “me”, resulting in health benefits for me, which benefit the whole family. Putting yourself last might not be the hangup of most users, but it is mine: with my busy friends and family, having an electronic, well-intentioned nudge in my pocket (the Productive app) is good during this time of life.  

The Productive app lets me set up and modify task lists for morning and evening routines and free floating daily or weekly tasks. It gives me pop-ups - yes, they’re irritating when I’m off-task, but that’s the point. I love the calm, black background color, bright colors and quirky symbols for tasks. I love the flexibility of changing my tasks as some become habits needing no reminders. And of course I can define new tasks as part of my routines to acquire habits I hope to eventually do automatically. I suppose it’s the sticker chart I never had as a kid.  

Again, in the cognitive assault of perimenopausal sleep deprivation, I rely on the Productive app to do what used to be super easy. It reminds me of the background stuff that has to chug along for life to be smooth and satisfying - stuff I never used to have to list out.  For example, the app is supporting an earlier bedtime, longer walks with the dog (I need more steps), making the time to enjoy my tween, and time spent actually preparing vegetables rather than time capsuling them in the fridge drawers - these are all tasks I define ranging from the trivial to the emotional high stakes stuff.  Checking off the tasks on my phone provides moments of reflection during my days, which helps me file away those good times with my kids, the dog (and all those fresh veg). The app is my medium-term background memory. Best of all, it highlights “streaks” of completing tasks consecutively: this is like an electronic pat on the back, which right now I relish. 

Will I keep using the Productive app when perimenopause ends and I’ve got a new normal?  Wrong question: it’s super when I need it during this transition, which is right now!

title: Helpful for Reminding/Bad for Data Tracking

I’ve been using this to set goals to increase meal prepping, eating cooked meals from home and working out. I love the actual checklist part, but the way the app tracks data doesn’t make sense. If you complete all of your daily goals you get a filled in bubble for the day. If you have a goal set for 3x/week, the days that you do that goal will be filled in but the days that you don’t remain hollow. I think at the end of the week if all of your weekly goals are met that all of the bubbles for that week should become filled in to show you had a perfect week. 

Additionally, I don’t understand how the streaks work (yes I read it in the app). Sometimes if you skip a habit or don’t do it, it will break your streak (which makes sense), but then I’ve also had it happen where if I have perfect days in a row somehow my streak has been broken. 

I really wish the data collection piece made more sense so I could get a more accurate picture of my hard work.

title: Awesome!
body: I love this app for tracking habits. The premium version is well worth the price, especially if you consider the cost per month of the annual option. I’ve been trying to start a bullet journal, but have struggled with motivating myself to go through and physically set up the format myself to track each habit, with this app it does all the work for me and has a nice design. I wish there was a little bit more flexibility with scheduling monthly habits, like if you could pick an exact day of the month when something needs to be done, or the number of times per month you’d want to do something, similar to the layout when setting weekly goals. Another feature I’d like to see is the ability to “overachieve” on a goal. Like if I set my gym goal as a minimum of 3 times a week, it would be nice to be able to mark it done if I go a fourth time in order to track progress and help reevaluate goals later on. I’d especially like it if this was a feature able to be turned on or off depending on each habit. Overall this is a great and easy to use app that helps me stay motivated and productive.

body:

I love the soothing charcoal backdrop and how you can customize every goal — from everything between daily and monthly in frequency, down to the color and icon associated with every goal. Goals can be any number of times per day/week/month, and you can assign them for a general time or for morning, afternoon, and evening.

Spring for the premium, it’s worth it. Getting to see your current streak of days with all habits completed, your best streak on record, and your total number of “perfect” days is so motivating.

title: Very Helpful and Encouraging
body: I don't often take time to write reviews, but I am sincerely enjoying this help! It has been so helpful and easy to use. I love how easy to customize this, and if you miss or skip a goal for whatever reason its not degrading. Rather it encourages you to keep going, and do what you can to succeed with whatever size goal/task/daily chore/project/new habit you recorded. I have tried other apps similar before and have been very disappointed, and then ended up losing interest and feeling more defeated by not getting something done. If you are a personality where you need to record your tasks or enjoy the satisfaction of crossing something else off from your day this is for you! I will admit that in the free version I only had the ability to record 2 goals/habits, which was not close to what I was hoping for. The company offered a timed promotion that Im not sure if it was only over the holiday or just as a new user I got a chance to upgrade too. However, I decided to give it a shot as it was only $12 for the full year which was easily affordable and I am really loving the fact I did. I highly recommend!

title: Great app for building/maintaining good habits
body:
I read “The Power of Habit” and wanted an app that would help me build good habits. You need a trigger and a reward for each one. While you are taking the time to naturally build these (eg, the trigger, such as going into the bathroom in the morning triggering several habits in a routine; the reward, such as a great trip to the dentist because you’ve been flossing), the app provides an easy trigger and reward system. 

The trigger is the notifications. I have turned off ALL other badge notifications. The first new habit I am committed to building is responding to this app / tracking my daily habits. Even if tracking means I mark the habit as “skipped” for the day. I am recording the data and setting goals for the year. 

The reward (again, this is scaffolding until my new habits’ natural rewards take over) is the feeling of accomplishment from tracking the data / marking things “done.”

100% completion on my daily workout habit is my big goal. 80% completion on everything else is my other goal. I will not change my set of habits all year - I’m trying to automate these behaviors, so consistency is key! December of next year I will think about what I want to change for the following year, practice all month, and set a new 100% goal. 

In 3 months I have a reminder set to review my notes from Power of Habit, along with my data from this app, and look for areas of improvement (as well as celebrations!) I imagine I will set another reminder after that to check in on my progress again in another 3 months. Humans are good about planning the next 90 day period but much longer than that, and the reminder won’t mean much. 

Hope this has been helpful for someone out there! And thank you to the developers for this great app!!

title: Okay but Very Very Basic
body:
Update: I would like to add to this after using this app for six months. The devs do not care about the users. The only reason I bought this subscription is so I could export my habits. You cannot do that at all! Yours notes are not in the back up! So if you get a new phones you’ll lose them. 

It’s a worse app than I thought; at least for me. What is the point of tracking habits if they can’t be exported. They might as well not recorded. 

————

So when I first installed and it asked for 19.99$ subscription pa I just quit it. I don’t have space for subscriptions anymore. I would happily pay 20$ as a one off but I’m not paying it again next year. 

Having said that it is a good app. It is evident that time and though was spend in building this. But not a subscription. Sorry. 

So a few days later they gave a limited time 50% offer which bought on an impulse without having tried the app for a few days. I was ready to delete it just didn’t got around to it. But then they said 9.99$ for a year. This doesn’t mean the price was just too high I just desperately needed an app which does what this does to an extend and don’t have the time to develop one myself atm. I still would not consider subscription at a lower price. And I will definitely not renew this. 

So on to the review, the subscription model gets me going... it is good concept. The UX is well enough designed though it can be improved to be more fluid eg there’s no 3D Touch support, sliding back doesn’t work, pop ups don’t close with slides/flicks or taps etc. Most people might not notice these things but I do. I’m lazy. 

I haven’t  had the chance to try out the stats parts but it seems just a simple chain. I’ll export all my habit when I need to analyse them so I don’t mind the simplicity. 

I imagine the dev just added notes part in the end doesn’t consider that an average user uses it often enough. I do. So that need to properly incorporated. 

There’s loads more quicks. So it might fit your needs but if it doesn’t it doesn’t. Luckily they at least let you try it before you buy. 

It’s things like these that dev can’t be blamed for not thinking about them but should be blamed because this has a subscription model.

PS: Dev if you read this, know I mean no disrespect or disparage you or your work. It is good. You should be proud of it. And thank you for the 50% off offer. You’ve given me time to build my own and knowledge of what I need. Don’t worry it’ll pretty different and won’t be published. It would have a very  niche use

title: A little disappointed but good design!
body:
This app is amazing. But only if you’re able to afford premium. The free version only makes you able to track 3 habits, which is very unrealistic (at least to teenagers- we really need to get our lives together). I feel like a need to buy the premium to actually enjoy this app but I can barely afford my gas money. 

If any of the developers are seeing this, PLEASE increase the number of habits available for free. At least to 5 or so. So many college students want to use this app to try and organize their life but only having 3 free habits available isn’t enough. We’re forced to look for other apps that offer many more habits, but in much less quality.

Despite only using this app for 20 minutes I still gotta give it 3 stars because the design is outstanding. Everything is so organized and easily accessible. The small things you can do with each habit put this app superior to all other habit-tracking apps, but so many of us decide not to use it because there’s only 3 free habits. If anything, at least make the subscription options cheaper. I know there’s many people who use this app already and pay for premium just fine, but there’s a ton of money-challenged people out there that really want to use this app so much :))). I know I can just put in my three top habits to track but I can’t exactly choose, haha. They all seem important to me. 

If you’re out there living a stable life and income, this app is for you! It’s definitely the #1 habit-tracking app if you pay for premium. From what I hear, it’s totally worth it.

I’m a broke college student - I can’t afford to lose that money. The option to unsubscribe NEEDS to be more available and user-friendly.

Edit: I’m fully aware that manually unsubscribing from the app is necessary, as is with most apps, but there is literally no option to opt out under those settings - the button in red font at the bottom of the page that should be there is nonexistent, but it’s present in the other apps I have. As I said above, I already tried to unsubscribe but eventually assumed that I wasn’t going to be charged since every other app I had, and the format of the page in the tutorial, included a very obvious “unsubscribe” button. I’d just like to know what my options are for getting my money refunded.

title: Kinda Good App.
body:
In the past few days I’ve been looking for an app that could serve as a calendar and time tracker. After trying out various calendars, I’ve decided that the original calendar that came with my iPad is the best and most straightforward one and requires the least time spent on scheduling. However it doesn’t track my time on my activities. So I got this app to track my time. 

What I find this app to be missing, is a calendar where I can see my schedule as I make it. For a person with ADHD, it is hard to visualize a schedule in the mind, it’s kinda like doing the “bara book bara boom” then never go on that vacation because I forgot about the whole thing. In the same manner I can schedule my intentions and even if there is a sound to remind me, if I can’t look at it on a visual timeline, the sound just feels like a reminder for something I’ve already forgotten and my self confidence gets shattered. Also, I can’t send my schedule from Productive to my Apple Calendar but I can send it to Apple Notes, which makes no sense. There is absolutely zero purpose for my calendar to hang out there in a form of a text “to read later”.

Another thing is, that you can only put down things you will definitely do again and again over time at the exact same time. So this app is excellent for reminding me to take my medication. But if I want to clean my kitchen floor, I only have the option to schedule it with the same time and same day in in mind for the future. There is no “one time” scheduling on Productive. I could make a schedule for repeating unspecified “house chores” but then I won’t remember or know which housework I want to do when the time comes, so I have to use my calendar for that.  I usually make plans for such things only a day or two in advance and these chores don’t follow any time pattern. 

What Productive is good for, are things that you want to be sure you are doing at the same time and same day every time you do them. It can be every day, same days a week, or for example, activities done every Wednesday each month. So what I use it for, is going to sleep at the same time every night (I need discipline to go to sleep), waking up at the same time every day at the same time and make sure my dog and I take our medications on time every day. I have two other activities on Productive that I want to make sure I make happen every day for 6 hours, 5 times a week. I would recommend that you don’t over schedule your Productive with activities, because you will still need time slots for your calendar. If you load all your activities on Productive, you will live like a robot. There are things that I need to do once in a while and they can’t interfere with activities on Productive. Since I live in a remote rural area I have to spend a day each month shopping for- and stocking on food to last for awhile. This shopping trip does not always fall on the same day or date and interferes with my Productive schedule. I guess that means I have to cheat once a month because there is no flexibility in the schedule on this app.

What is really good about Productive is that it’s simple to use (although the usefulness is quite limited in my opinion) and it is Siri activated. 

The improvements I would most like to see is: 1) the ability to sync this app with my Apple calendar, 2) a bit more control over the timing of the schedules I create in Productive.

title: Missing obvious features
body:
I purchased the premium version. It’s missing obvious features. For example, it doesn’t allow you to connect your items with the attainment of overall goals. Which is a big mistake. Because it’s overall goals that keep us motivated! I want to see progress towards a goal, not simply streaks. 

Also, there’s no way to set actual times to accomplish your tasks. You simply have morning, afternoon, and evening. Nor is there a way to set tasks that require many instances of completion during a single day. For example drink 10 cups of water spread out over the course of a day. The app Daily Tracker allows you to do this, but that app also fails by not allowing users to establish overall goals and track progress towards that goal. 

These tracker apps annoy me by not really advancing their functionality. 

There are many other ideas I have that would make this app flexible and a true resource. As it stands, the premium version isn’t very good. Might as well be free, but I guess they’re selling how pretty and easy to use it is. And that’s true, it is pretty, and easy to use.

title: Great App
body:
I find this app highly motivating to help me establish new habits in my life. I love the simplicity of the design. 

This app has literally helped save my life. I’m a recovering drug addict, who lived for years practicing unhealthy habits. As a part of my program of recovery, I began to utilize your app to teach myself how to practice healthy habits. I made a list of ten things that I was going to try and do every day and entered them into the app. 

While I can’t say that I’ve completed all of them every day, I can say that I’ve completed at least 90% of them every day. Out of the past 28 days, I’ve performed all ten habits on 24 days. Those healthy habits have gone a long way to helping me stay clean for the last month. 

Many people, who I share my experience with about using your app, ask what ten habits do I try to do every day. I’ll refrain from sharing that list, because I believe the habits we choose to shape our lives are personal.

By using your app, I’ve come to realize that some things in my life are nonnegotiable, such as, staying clean. Thank you.

title: Underhanded
body:
I use this app daily, and I do see how it is helping me be more productive. However, they’re a bit cheeky when it comes to adding a habit. Supposably, you are allowed to have five free habits, which for a long time, I did. I myself whittled it down and then up and down again over time, and it wasn’t a problem. Until this past month. Now, I have three and want to add, but whenever I try to add one to the three I currently have, it takes me to a page that only gives me the option to pay for unlimited habits. I have looked all over the entire app repeatedly, and there is no option to add a habit any other way then to pull down, and when I do, as I said, it gives me no option but to add a free habit. I contacted support on this, and here was the reply (no explanation, no apology, no offer to restore my original 5 habit allowance): 
Hello Lily,
Thanks for your feedback.
Unfortunately some users might indeed have only 3 free habits in the free version.
Thank you for using our app.
Best regards,
Natallia

(Addendum: as for developer’s response to this review seen below, they clearly misread my review. I was getting 5 free habits for several months, and suddenly & randomly, those 5 free were limited down to 3. Nowhere in the free version did it indicate that this would happen after several months, mind you, not after a one free month trial. I am currently in touch with Apalon support, and twice now, they’ve admitted responsibility, acknowledging that the issue was within the app dysfunction. But it took many back and forth emails to get to this point. And now, I see the reply below.)

title: Compound Effect!!
body:
This app has totally helped me stay on track with my habits (battle rhythm). I definitely see the compound effect of staying consistent and not missing simple habits. For example, reading, clear email or saying hello to a stranger each day. Awesome reminders as soon as you can streamline your planning and make it happen.

After gaining some streaks, you are more self-accountable to completing habits and I started seeing more results in my life and business. 

Excellent app for people who just want to get on auto-pilot for success. But it also matters what your goals are. Once I get on auto-pilot with one habit, I take it off/create a new one.

title: Cut free version’s options in half — unhappy
body:
I deleted this. I do NOT appreciate this recent trend toward subscription models — it’s unsustainable for me and feels ridiculous for an app to charge a continuous fee for something I don’t consider essential. Handy? Yes. Crucial to my wellbeing to the point I’m going to shell out money every single month for the rest of my life? No. Would I pay a one time fee? Absolutely. 

I was okay with the free version with the 5 available habits, but after the most recent update this was decreased to THREE! I’ve been using the app for years, on the fence about supporting a subscription model, and then they slice the free options in half. I’m unhappy with this decision. 

I cannot afford subscriptions to all the apps I use. However, I am perfectly okay with adds for “lite” free versions or paying a one time fee for a quality app. If the pricing model changes to a one time fee I will happily pay and redownload. 

As of now I do not recommend.

body:

I give this app three stars because, aside from the stats and the color coordinated symbols, I could easily perform every function through the free Apple Reminders app. Productive only allows three habits in the free version and charges at least $2 per month for unlimited access, depending on subscription length. For that, I am opting to take this idea to the free Reminders app and build my own pseudo habit tracker.

title: Quite a good app
body: I especially appreciate this app, since the calendar it has tracks when you do things and when you don’t do things. This gives you a satisfying cross-off of the days of the week you do the things you planned, making you feel compelled to keep up the task instead of putting it off another day. That being said, all of the features (in the free version at least) besides reminders can be done using a regular calendar, which would give you an even more satisfying cross-off since it is being done physically. However, I would still recommend this app, for people who are still struggling with procrastination, since it isn’t the laziness but rather the will, and personally the will has kept me going with this app. The only downside is that I think the not free version is quite a bit expensive, especially for a mere habit tracking app, and especially considering that all of the features it has and offers in the paid version could be done with other apps that are free (like apps that come with an iPhone). Nevertheless, this is still an amazing app and it has helped me with habit tracking.

author: Keegan Cooke

title: My Main App
body:
I have paranoid schizophrenia, and having a stable routine along with medication and therapy is essential to my recovery.  This is hands down the best app for creating and maintaining a daily self care routine.  Being schizophrenic it is hard to stick with a routine.  I am always forgetting what I need to be doing.  Not anymore with this app.  I use this app to remind me of the things I need to do each day.  For projects I use Things 3, for one time reminders I use the standard reminders app, and for appointments I use the basic calendar.  I keep these four apps in a folder called Daily. If I see a number over the folder, I know that something needs to be done.

What I like most about this app is nothing has a time that is set in stone.  There are three periods:  morning, afternoon, and evening.  This gives me needed flexibility, in case I am having a bad day.  Also these periods keep me from becoming overwhelmed by looking at a whole days worth of tasks.  (Although you can look at the full day if you need to).  There is also a satisfying sound when you swipe a task complete.  This app has worked wonders in my day to day life living with schizophrenia. If you don’t have a serious mental illness this app will still be extremely handy.  If you do have a serious mental illness it is a necessity.

title: Missing one key feature
body:
This app is very good, as the other reviews attest. However, it has one major flaw in my opinion.

Let's say you have a habit you want to do 3x per week. Now, if you are having a great week maybe you decide to go for 4x that week. No joy. In this app, once you hit your goal of 3x the habit effectively disappears for the rest of the week. So, it is impossible to track any extra days.

I suspect this is what other people are referring to when they say that this app is useless for tracking. The fix (IMO) is to let a person choose whether to show or hide a habit once the weekly goal has been met. I can see where the "right" answer may vary from habit to habit. So, ideally you could set this as appropriate on each habit.

body: I downloaded the free trial of this app and while it’s got a nice principle function, there were some features the app was lacking, in my opinion. You have to cancel your subscription through a link that’s not easily found in the app, that takes you to the Apple support site and you have to cancel through that platform instead of within the app itself. If you do not cancel before the 7 day trial is up, you are automatically charged the premium subscription fee and that purchase cannot be canceled (ie no refund). Usually apps will refund the automatic charge if you cancel within a day or so of when the free trial ends. This was not the case, and I feel like I was swindled into paying $20 that is apparently non-refundable, which is extremely unsettling. Beware of this.

title: This is a killer app
body:
I am beginning to love Productive. It is a customizable app that makes it easier for you to build and stick to habits.

I started trying this out for a week and didn’t use it very much, because the app is really valuable if you dedicate time to customizing it and using it. When my free week expired, it auto-bought the year membership, so I thought, fine, let me give it a second try. Boy am I glad I did.

I use Productive between 1-3 times a day, which makes sense: the app has 3 built in reminders to do tasks (morning, afternoon, and evening). It has been a tool I’ve used to put into action the morning and evening routines I want to do on a daily basis. It has also helped me figure out what habits I am building effectively and which ones I am not, because I see how many days in a row I’ve done something and it’s a signal to me that my system is broken if I lapse more than a day in a row. It also helped me to realize that being specific and actionable is super important because there is nothing to “do” on an item that is general and vague.

All in all, I’ve started to recommend this app to my clients and think if someone is a self-starter, they will appreciate this and might even love it!

The one thing I hope Productive improves is adding more images to assign to habits. They have a large list, but to boost it further would be great.

Bottom line: worth the $20!

title: Great app!
body:
I'm 16 and I got this app to keep track of chores and other daily habits I often forget. It's exactly what I needed. I'm not trying to schedule my day down to the minute or even the hour. And I needed an app flexible enough that as long as I complete my habit that day, it doesn't break my streak, but still keeping certain habits to certain times of day.
I like that you can schedule an individual habit for multiple times a day instead of having to create the same habit 3 times, each time scheduling a different time. I also enjoy how customizable it is, how you can choose the icon, color and order of the habits. My favorite thing about the app is the general scheduling. There are 3 times to schedule a habit to; morning, afternoon and evening. And you can choose between which times each of these apply. Even if I miss a habit during its schedules time, it isn't counted as missed until the day is over, which keeps my motivation for the streaks up.  It's the perfect level of simplicity for me.
My only complaint is that I have to pay a subscription for more habits! I don't really care about whatever else comes with premium. I love this app and it's exactly what I need but I can't pay a subscription. If it was a one-time fee for premium forever then I could do that. Even if it was $20 as long as it was just once. Otherwise, this app is just about perfect for me.

In productive all I can see is if I had a perfect day or a partially complete day. But for me there’s a big difference between completing 10% of my habits for the day and 90%, but they both count as partially complete days!

The ads to subscribe are near ever present! Why not give consumers a way to buy it once for a higher price. It looks like they can raise the rate any old time they choose (fine print) meaning you will have to pay more or get a new app. Highly annoying for me as a consumer. It’s a good app. However the way they are forcing ads on you is annoying. 

DON’T SUPPORT THIS TREND. 
Please rate all these subscription type apps with one star and then just don’t buy them. If you support subscription apps soon that is all we will have. As consumers you have a voice. They won’t give you a choice later if they want to raise rates. This type of pricing is not consumer friendly and should not be supported by the marketplace.

title: Fun and simple but limited and many ads
body:
This app appealed to me because it looked colorful and fun. It is those things. I found it easy to use and liked the icons and color choices. 

One downside for me is that it’s limited to three times of a day. I did add a few regular reminders. Thing is, I’ve been using My Home Routines for several years and segment my days a bit more finely than three parts. Using emoticons to label my tasks is a bit more work but does add some fun and color. 

Not wanting to abandon Productivity just yet, I thought to use it just for new habits that I want to embrace. As I was deleting the tasks already put in and adding a new one, I found the ads for their subscription to be intrusive. At one point my work was interrupted by a new screen with one. Seems like half the menu is about subscribing. 

Even though I expect ads in a free app, I don’t expect them to interfere. And as a personal choice, I prefer a one time purchase to an ongoing subscription. I would likely buy a paid version of the app. Instead I’m uninstalling it 🙁

We talked back and forth and he was greatly receptive to my suggestions, and I just couldn't wait for future updates that included my ideas! 

It is very rare to find an app that perfectly meets your needs, and even rarer to find one with a developer who is so open to feedback and so kind.

Well, imagine my surprise one day, after updating my favorite app (which I did pay for), excitedly opening it to see what improvements have been made, and all of a sudden it's telling me that to do pretty much anything, I must SUBSCRIBE for a monthly fee!! Disappointment doesn't even begin to describe it. 

I feel as though the dev let down each and every customer who supported him from the very beginning. I take it as a personal slap in the face, after purchasing the app, utilizing it from the beginning and having such positive correspondence with the dev. It just is not right.

author: Lena_cruz

title: Hooray!
body:
Finally an app that actually motivates me to stick to my goals, whether they’re daily or yearly. I rarely write reviews on apps but I couldn’t not write one for this app. I wanted to give it 4 1/2 stars because my one complaint is pretty small but I either can’t figure it out or it’s not possible. 

As I said, this app has helped with my motivation to get things done quite a bit. I’m usually a procrastinator but the idea of breaking a streak because I’m feeling lazy drives me crazy, which encourages me to just get it done. It’s a really great psychological trick and it’s really what sets this app apart from other reminder apps (and I’ve tried quite a few because right now I’m still writing my to-do lists and reminders on paper every day and I’m trying to get away from that and switch to my phone and other Apple devices.  

As I said I do have one minor complaint, and it’s that you can’t add any notes or additional information until you’ve already completed the task. This frustrated me a couple times and left me having to keep the additional information in a separate app, which is not ideal. Pretty minor, but if it is possible and I’m just missing it could someone let me know? And if I’m correct about this... developers? :) could you maybe allow it in a future update? If Productive had that capability, it would be a 5 star rating from me. 

Overall though I’d highly recommend it. I’m only still in my week long trial but I intend to keep the paid full version (totally a reasonable cost for a year which says a lot about how worth it the app is because I’m super cheap when it comes to any purchases, especially electronic ones). 

So try it out, you’ve got nothing to lose. Try the upgraded paid version for at least the week’s free trial you’re offered to see if it’s worth it for you, too. And if it is, I think the cost for a year is pretty justifiable.
author: EhThroughZed

title: Nice app but subscription is ridiculous.
body: The user interface in Productive is laid out well and I actually prefer it to other apps like HabitBull but their subscription structure is ridiculous and I refuse to rent software rather than own it. This trend across the software industry is poisonous and in every instance that a developer has changed to a subscription only based fee structure I have sought an alternative app or, in cases like Adobe products, I’ve either downgraded to inferior versions like Photoshop Elements or have gone against my own ethical standards and pirated a piece of software because the developer took away my choice to own it.  I hate piracy, and in the case of Photoshop I have learned to settle using Photoshop Elements rather than a pirated full version, but the amount of revenue Adobe and other developers have missed out on from me is substantial due to their own greed. I understand that some consumers prefer a subscription model and they should certainly have that choice but it should be a choice rather than a requirement due to the choice of ownership being taken from them. Back to Productive... I would have definitely bought it for $4 when it was that price but I just learned about it. I would gladly spend $10-$20 or even more to own it now but since it is now only available to rent I have chosen to use HabitBull as my daily habit tracking app. I guess developers of apps like Productive feel that the revenue lost from driving away customers like me is outweighed by the increase in revenue from their subscription only fees. It’s a depressing trend and one that I hope dies out in favor of both purchase and subscription choices being the standard. The sad thing is that I’d have never even considered writing this review had they given me a choice of purchasing or renting the app.  I encourage every consumer to keep up the pressure on developers to offer that choice.  The developers of Productive have lost me as a potential customer as long as they do not offer a purchase option but the next company has a choice. Do they want my money or not? Thanks for reading.

title: Promising, but some definite flaws.
body:
I’ve been a premium user of this app for over 2 years and try to use it regularly, but it has a few flaws that don’t seem to be budging.

1. You can’t snooze a habit.
If you don’t get to a habit on it’s assigned day, you can either skip it or leave it incomplete. There’s no option to snooze for any amount of time (e.g., next day). A 3D Touch or long press on an active task to snooze until tomorrow would be great!

2. No option to hide completed habits.
If you have several habits on a given day (or in a given window, say, afternoon), there’s no way hide these. So you see your greyed out completed habits rather than those you have yet to do.
A simple toggle switch atop the interface to hide completed habits would solve this. Then if you wanted to view details or undo a completed habit, you could toggle the switch and do so, but by default, these should be hidden to avoid clogging up the interface.

3. Earlier incomplete habits vanish when the time window ends. (App badge and screen).
Say you’re running late, and some of your morning habits aren’t done by the time afternoon roles around. Those habits will vanish from the interface, and the badge icon counter for undone habits no longer includes them. There’s a small link to view them at the bottom, but if you have multiple prior periods (say it’s evening and you have a habit incomplete in both morning and afternoon), you have to view all habits, and this of course includes the completed ones (see above issue).
An option to always display incomplete habits after their time windows have passed would be much appreciated. The “do anytime today” is great, but there are tons of times users need “plan to do every morning, but even if the morning ends, I still want to do it”

4. No iPhone X support yet, but I didn’t dock points for this, it’s a new screen layout. Just would be nice (:

title: $4 total -> $12 -> $20 subscription?
body:
Overall, I like this app.  What I don’t like is the trend I am seeing (read the comments).  We have gone from a fixed price app, to an app that cost $12-13 a year to something that costs $20 a year using a subscription.  Has the value increased at the same pace?  Are new features added monthly?

If you paid for a subscription (especially one costing $20/year (that’s the new price)), help us out by sharing your experience in the comments.  Do you think this is worth that much?

Otherwise, if you want a fixed price app, check out Things.  You can create recurring tasks/todos that behave just like “habits” and synchronize that across all your devices.  Overall, I am left thinking that this app is overpriced for what you get and not worth the perpetual payments for the extra features.  The free version doesn’t do enough to be viable on its own.

***Developer Responses?***
The canned responses in all the comments don’t address the constant price increases as they relate to newly added value.  Share your thoughts to let people like me know if there is value based on your experience given the current price, $20/year recurring costs.

title: Nice app but lacking some important features.
body:
I’m a premium user of this app, and overall it’s nice looking and moderately functional. My biggest complaint is that it’s almost useless for data tracking. 

I meditate pretty much every day, but I consider doing it at least five days a week a success. So I went ahead and set the goal for five days a week. I meditated five days in a row, and suddenly I’ve lost the option to track it anymore for that week. Say I meditate every day for a week, I can’t track that under the five days setting. Meaning if I want to go back in time to see what days I usually miss, notice any patterns in the data—I’m out of luck. If I set it to the every day setting, and I miss a day, I lose my streak in the habit. 

Either I set it to five days, and I can’t keep accurate data records, or I set it to a week and I lose the motivation of maintaining a streak. It’s a really big flaw in the app and it would be nice to have it fixed. At least an option to allow a user to go over the set number of days would be nice, even if it wasn’t the default setting.

title: Lots of good, but one real flaw
body:
I love that the free version lets you get a real feel for the app before you buy.  I love that you can make your own habits, add notes to them, and order them how you want, with your day being divided into morning, afternoon and evening so you can see everything clearly.

I can't believe it doesn't have a function to allow you to see the habits you have to accomplish on any future days, only past days.

Also, you'd think they'd have a way for you to have tasks repeat every other day, and also on certain days of the month. It literally only lets you add tasks that repeat "at the beginning of the month or the middle of the month or the end of the month".

There's an app called motivated moms that is similar.  It allows you to look ahead at habits coming up for the future.  So, you can look at tomorrow and see: OK that's the day I'm trying to go to the gym to do weightlifting and then I'm also trying to meditate that day and I wanted to use that day to clean the living room.  It really helps to see all the things you plan to do on a regular schedule but not the same each day, or even each week (like, I'm trying to plan the next month's expenses on the last Sunday of each month). 

Motivated moms also allows you to schedule things for every other day.

The only thing I don't like about motivated moms is that you cannot rearrange the order of the habits. That's a real dealbreaker for me.

I also prefer the way this app looks over the motivated moms app. I hope they fix the above issues in a version in the future soon.

title: Beautiful and useful but missing a few things
body:
I really like this app in some ways, but it falls short in some important areas. I am not thrilled to have to pay $14 a year for an app that is missing features I think it should have but I am willing to support the developers for now hoping that the subscription model will work and the missing features are added. 

First what I like: 
* This is a beautiful looking app. That is important to me. 
* Helpful as a habit builder with the reminders, showing streaks, etc. 
* The morning, afternoon, evening layout works well
* Ability to set multiple reminders is great
* Ability to set multiple (up to 3) times a day is useful
* The boost feature to help you work on new habits

What is missing: 
* Setting specific times for habits would be nice 
* To set a weekly habit on a specific day, you need to actually set it as daily and then pick the day of week by deselecting all other days. That is not intuitive and I would like to be able to set something as "weekly" and pick the day. 
* Monthly habits should allow you to pick a specific day of the month. I do not see a way to do this. There is no work around like there is with weekly tasks. 
* The interface is beautiful but the flow relies too much on "back" and "menu". I think swiping (away from habits area) would be nicer, or a consistent menu on the bottom. 
* I would also like to see a way to click on a day through a calendar. (Similar to week view at the bottom but showing more days, and letting you look at future days.) 
* Syncing so I could use this app on my iPad or elsewhere and use the same data 
* Web interface 

The last 2 items are really important to me. Especially the syncing. This is what makes me willing to pay a subscription price for an app. Otherwise it should be a one-off price. If this does not change by the next time my subscription fee comes up, I will not be renewing.

body: I was looking at this app and the concept is amazing. And it's so simple. It's what I loved the most. My folks hate to download or try new apps because they find it difficult to understand or adjust to their preferences. Their constantly complaining about how there to old and technology left them behind. And yet this app's concept seems to prove them wrong. It shows that there are still apps out there for anyone. For both the young and the old alike. Plus they give you the option to write in your own personal habits, activities, etc. They even have a journal. I have not really played with it yet. But after looking at it and checking out the upgrade, I had paid the $3.99. Honestly I give away that amount on stuff I don't normally need. But this is an app that most ppl like myself can use. I give 5 stars based on the concept. I will be writing a second review next week. I will be utilizing this app all week as if my daily routine won't function without it, plus I will be adding some extra activities that I never seem to have time for or I just simple forget. Then I will rewrite a new review and let you know how well the app worked for me. I do say this much, if this app can help me, them this should be the next big thing.

title: I was skeptical at first

I thought I would just try it out and probably give up on it within a week but it has completely changed my daily habits for the better. I've been using it for over a month now. It helped me remember when to go to bed so I got enough sleep, when to get ready for work so I would stop being late, when to take my medication so I could properly function, I am even sticking to a vegetarian diet (finally!!) after years of trying and failing to commit. Seriously, I highly recommend this app for people who have trouble keeping up with necessary, beneficial, daily routines (like my ADHD self).

title: Exactly what I have been looking for!
body:
Edit: I hope the app creator sees this! I have loved this app for a long time. There is one thing that I desperately wish it could do, however.  I really wish that I could see what's on the agenda for the next day.  I use this app not only for habits, but as a daily planner.  Not being able to see what exactly is on the agenda for the next day is a bummer.

Original review: I have spent the past year downloading (and often buying) habit/daily chore apps before then uninstalling them in disappointment. I really liked the idea of a gamified habit app, but after trying several, they just didn't have the deeper features I wanted which caused me to quit using them after some time. This app, is so much nicer. Its beautiful, so customizable, and a real joy to use. And it has features, such as streaks and graphs to help you visualize your success so that you will want to keep it up.  Really cool. The only thing I wish it had was a separate section where I could make one-time lists, such as a grocery list. Aside from working on habits, I usually have several separate lists going on, depending on if I need groceries, what bills are coming due, etc. I like to keep that separate from my habits. For now I either use notes or another list app, but it would be really cool to see that feature added in this app.  Aside from that, I am very impressed. I bought the full version because it is so worth it. Keep up the good work!

title: Changing my Life
body:
This app is wonderful, and for me, life changing! 

I love that it breaks habits into morning, afternoon, and evening habits, and it reminds me to do them. :D it shows me my success streaks, which encourages me to keep going. I'm having lots of success with this app.

It even helped me to break bad habits, like biting my nails. I set the habit "Don't bite nails" for three times a day, and after just a week of being reminded thrice daily, I was doing so much better! Just being reminded of my intention to not bite my nails was all I needed to break a 15 year bad habit. 

One thing I'd love to see added is a way to take notes on habits. When I miss a habit, I wish there was a way to take a memo of "why?" For example, if I bit my nails one day, it would be nice to take a memo: "got bored after lunch" or "feeling anxious about presentation."

title: Great motivation and excellent customer service!
body:
I downloaded productive because I was struggling to stay committed to doing my physical therapy for a torn hip labrum every day as my PT instructed. I downloaded the app a few days into my month long challenge of doing my therapy everyday, and I found it really helped me to stay motivated when I could check off and visualize my completed exercise routine on the well-designed and aesthetically pleasing app. I contacted their support team to see if there was a way to retroactively add in the days I had completed my exercise routine before I had downloaded the app, and they were very friendly and helpful in helping me get it all sorted out. I would definitely recommend this app as a way to stay motivated if you have goals you struggle to keep up with! 

My only recommendation would be to create more advanced goal setting features. For example, I would like to tell the app that my overall goal is to complete a month of doing PT every day, so it could provide me with information about how many more days I have to go and what percent of the goal I have achieved. It would also me nice to be able to put in and see information about why this is your goal (for me, it is life without chronic hip pin and avoiding hip surgery) and any rewards you plan to give yourself if you obtain the goal (I'm taking myself out to a nice dinner after my month-long challenge is complete). Obviously these are things I know already, but it would be fun to integrate them into the app and see reminders of why my goals are important to me.
